````python
    return [cf_text("No", "bad"), cf_text("Yes", "good")]


def target_cf(target_name: str) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
    """Green at or above a named target, amber below it."""
    return [
        {"type": "cell", "criteria": ">=", "value": f"={target_name}",
         "fmt": "good"},
        {"type": "cell", "criteria": "<", "value": f"={target_name}",
         "fmt": "warn"},
    ]


def rating_cf() -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
    return [
        {"type": "cell", "criteria": ">=", "value": 4.8, "fmt": "bold_good"},
        {"type": "cell", "criteria": ">=", "value": 4.5, "fmt": "good"},
        {"type": "cell", "criteria": ">=", "value": 4.0, "fmt": "warn"},
        {"type": "cell", "criteria": "<", "value": 4.0, "fmt": "bad"},
    ]


def yesno(note: str = "") -> Dict[str, Any]:
    return yes_no(note)


def score_validation(maximum: int = 5) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    return {
        "validate": "decimal",
        "criteria": "between",
        "minimum": 1,
        "maximum": maximum,
        "error_title": f"Rating 1-{maximum}",
        "error_message": f"Enter a rating from 1 (poor) to {maximum} "
                         "(excellent). Half stars are fine.",
    }


def pick(name: str, note: str = "") -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Drop-down fed by a defined name, with an optional hint bubble."""
    opts = dict(list_from(name))
    if note:
        opts["input_message"] = note
    return opts


def amount(minimum: float = 0, maximum: float = 1000000,
           note: str = "", decimal: bool = True) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Numeric entry check, with an optional hint bubble."""
    opts = dict(number_check(minimum, maximum, decimal))
    if note:
        opts["input_message"] = note
    return opts


def blank(trigger: str, body: str) -> str:
    """`=IF(trigger="","",body)` with the standard row placeholders."""
    return f'=IF({{{trigger}}}{{r}}="","",{body})'


def zero(trigger: str, body: str) -> str:
    """`=IF(trigger="",0,body)` - for columns that must never return "".

    Any column a `SUMPRODUCT`, `MAX(cond*range)` or calendar lookup reads
    has to be numeric on every single row, including the ones that do not
    apply, or Excel multiplies a number by an empty string and answers
    `#VALUE!`.
    """
    return f'=IF({{{trigger}}}{{r}}="",0,{body})'


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Cross sheet lookups.  Every one is blank-row safe and says what to do
# when the ID does not exist, because a typo in an ID is the single most
# common thing that goes wrong in a workbook like this.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def lookup(sheet: str, target: str, key_col: str, key: str,
           missing: str = "") -> str:
    """Generic `INDEX/MATCH` against any register, blank row safe."""
    return (f'=IF({{{key}}}{{r}}="","",IFERROR(INDEX([[{sheet}.'
            f'{target}]],MATCH({{{key}}}{{r}},'
            f'[[{sheet}.{key_col}]],0)),"{missing}"))')


def lookup_num(sheet: str, target: str, key_col: str, key: str) -> str:
    """Numeric `INDEX/MATCH` - 0 when the ID is missing or the cell empty.

    `INDEX` on an empty cell returns 0, not "", so numeric lookups are
    coerced with `*1` inside the `IFERROR` rather than compared to "".
    """
    return (f'=IF({{{key}}}{{r}}="","",IFERROR(INDEX([[{sheet}.'
            f'{target}]],MATCH({{{key}}}{{r}},'
            f'[[{sheet}.{key_col}]],0))*1,0))')


def lookup_num_zero(sheet: str, target: str, key_col: str, key: str) -> str:
    """As :func:`lookup_num`, but returns 0 rather than "" on a blank row."""
    return (f'=IF({{{key}}}{{r}}="",0,IFERROR(INDEX([[{sheet}.'
            f'{target}]],MATCH({{{key}}}{{r}},'
            f'[[{sheet}.{key_col}]],0))*1,0))')

def rank_desc(key: str, guard: str = '{name}{r}=""',
              header: str = "Rank", width: float = 9,
              note: str = "") -> Col:
    """Hidden dense rank, 1 = the biggest value in `key`.

    Ties are broken by row order, so the ranks come out 1, 2, 3 ... with
    no gaps and no duplicates.  Pages then read the nth row with an
    ordinary `MATCH(n, rank, 0)` - no array formula, so nothing in the
    workbook needs Ctrl+Shift+Enter.
    """
    return Col(f"{key}_rank", header, width, "int",
               formula=(f'=IF({guard},"",COUNTIFS({{{key}_first}}:'
                        f'{{{key}_last}},">"&{{{key}}}{{r}})+'
                        f'COUNTIFS({{{key}_first}}:{{{key}}}{{r}},'
                        f'{{{key}}}{{r}}))'),
               hidden=True, note=note or f"1 = the largest {key}.")


def rank_asc(key: str, guard: str = '{name}{r}=""',
             header: str = "Rank", width: float = 9,
             note: str = "") -> Col:
    """Hidden dense rank, 1 = the smallest value in `key`."""
    return Col(f"{key}_rank", header, width, "int",
               formula=(f'=IF({guard},"",COUNTIFS({{{key}_first}}:'
                        f'{{{key}_last}},"<"&{{{key}}}{{r}})+'
                        f'COUNTIFS({{{key}_first}}:{{{key}}}{{r}},'
                        f'{{{key}}}{{r}}))'),
               hidden=True, note=note or f"1 = the smallest {key}.")


def seq_key(parent: str, trigger: str = "") -> List[Col]:
    """Hidden `1, 2, 3 ...` within a parent, plus a `parent|n` key.

    Printables and per-parent summaries use `MATCH(parent & "|" & n, key, 0)`
    to pull the nth line of one record without an array formula.
    """
    trig = trigger or parent
    return [
        Col("seq", "Line", 6, "int",
            formula=blank(
                trig,
                f'COUNTIFS({{{parent}_first}}:{{{parent}}}{{r}},'
                f'{{{parent}}}{{r}})'),
            hidden=True),
        Col("key", "Key", 14, "text",
            formula=blank(trig, f'{{{parent}}}{{r}}&"|"&{{seq}}{{r}}'),
            hidden=True),
    ]


def days_until(date_cell: str) -> str:
    """Whole days from today to a date - negative once it has passed."""
    return f'({date_cell}-TodayDate)'


def countdown_band(days_cell: str) -> str:
    """Turn a day count into the band the dashboard groups on."""
    return (f'IF({days_cell}<0,"Past",'
            f'IF({days_cell}<=7,"This week",'
            f'IF({days_cell}<=30,"Next 30 days",'
            f'IF({days_cell}<=90,"1-3 months",'
            f'IF({days_cell}<=180,"3-6 months",'
            f'IF({days_cell}<=365,"6-12 months","Over a year"))))))')


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Cross sheet lookups - the four join keys
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# A Customer ID owns Property IDs. A Property ID owns Jobs. A Job owns
# its labour, its materials and its line on an invoice. Every one of
# those IDs is a drop-down somewhere, never a typed string, because a
# mistyped ID is a row that silently stops being part of the business.

def lookup_customer(target: str, key: str = "customer",
                    missing: str = "Not in Customer CRM") -> str:
    """A field from the customer record behind a Customer ID."""
    return lookup("Customer CRM", target, "id", key, missing)


def lookup_customer_num(target: str, key: str = "customer") -> str:
    return lookup_num("Customer CRM", target, "id", key)


def lookup_property(target: str, key: str = "property",
                    missing: str = "Not in Property Database") -> str:
    """A field from the property record behind a Property ID."""
    return lookup("Property Database", target, "id", key, missing)


def lookup_property_num(target: str, key: str = "property") -> str:
    return lookup_num("Property Database", target, "id", key)


def lookup_property_num_zero(target: str, key: str = "property") -> str:
    return lookup_num_zero("Property Database", target, "id", key)


def lookup_service(target: str, key: str = "service",
                   missing: str = "Not in Service Catalog") -> str:
    """A field from the service record behind a service name."""
    return lookup("Service Catalog", target, "name", key, missing)


def lookup_service_num(target: str, key: str = "service") -> str:
    return lookup_num("Service Catalog", target, "name", key)


def lookup_service_num_zero(target: str, key: str = "service") -> str:
    return lookup_num_zero("Service Catalog", target, "name", key)


def lookup_job(target: str, key: str = "job",
               missing: str = "Not in Job & Work Orders") -> str:
    """A field from the job record behind a Job ID."""
    return lookup("Job & Work Orders", target, "id", key, missing)


def lookup_job_num(target: str, key: str = "job") -> str:
    return lookup_num("Job & Work Orders", target, "id", key)


def lookup_crew(target: str, key: str = "employee",
                missing: str = "Not in Crew Database") -> str:
    """A field from the employee record behind an Employee ID."""
    return lookup("Crew Database", target, "id", key, missing)


def lookup_crew_num(target: str, key: str = "employee") -> str:
    return lookup_num("Crew Database", target, "id", key)


def lookup_contract(target: str, key: str = "contract",
                    missing: str = "") -> str:
    return lookup("Recurring Contracts", target, "id", key, missing)


def lookup_invoice_num(target: str, key: str = "invoice") -> str:
    return lookup_num("Invoice & Payments", target, "id", key)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The standard "who and where" columns
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def customer_col(key: str = "customer", header: str = "Customer",
                 width: float = 11, note: str = "") -> Col:
    """A Customer ID chosen from the live list, never typed."""
    return Col(key, header, width, "id",
               validate=pick(
                   "CustomerList",
                   "Pick the Customer ID. Add the customer on the "
                   "Customer CRM tab first if they are not listed."),
               note=note or "Pick from the list. A typed ID disconnects "
                            "this row from the customer.")


def property_col(key: str = "property", header: str = "Property",
                 width: float = 11, note: str = "") -> Col:
    return Col(key, header, width, "id",
               validate=pick(
                   "PropertyList",
                   "Pick the Property ID. Add it on the Property "
                   "Database tab first if it is not listed."),
               note=note or "Pick from the list. One customer can own "
                            "several properties.")


def service_col(key: str = "service", header: str = "Service",
                width: float = 24, note: str = "") -> Col:
    return Col(key, header, width, "text",
               validate=pick(
                   "ServiceList",
                   "Pick the service. Add it to the Service Catalog "
                   "tab first if it is not listed."),
               note=note or "Drives the default price and the time "
                            "estimate.")


def customer_name_col(key: str = "customer", width: float = 22) -> Col:
    return Col("customer_name", "Customer name", width, "text",
               formula=lookup_customer("name", key),
               note="Automatic. If it says 'Not in Customer CRM' the ID "
                    "is wrong.")


def property_address_col(key: str = "property", width: float = 30) -> Col:
    return Col("address", "Address", width, "text",
               formula=lookup_property("address", key),
               note="Automatic, from the Property Database.")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Status set tests - what a status MEANS, defined once
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def in_list(cell: str, values) -> str:
    """`(c="a")+(c="b")>0` - membership without OR().

    OR() evaluates every argument, so a blank cell in an argument that
    an earlier test should have ruled out still reaches the comparison.
    Adding booleans avoids it and is shorter in the formula bar.
    """
    terms = "+".join(f'({cell}="{value}")' for value in values)
    return f"({terms}>0)"


def is_open_job(cell: str) -> str:
    """A job that still has to happen."""
    return in_list(cell, OPEN_JOB_STATUSES)


def is_done_job(cell: str) -> str:
    """A job that was done - the only kind that earns anything."""
    return in_list(cell, DONE_JOB_STATUSES)


def is_catchup_job(cell: str) -> str:
    """Rained off or needing a revisit: work you still owe."""
    return in_list(cell, CATCHUP_JOB_STATUSES)


def is_won_quote(cell: str) -> str:
    return in_list(cell, WON_QUOTE_STATUSES)


def is_live_quote(cell: str) -> str:
    """Out with the customer and not yet answered."""
    return in_list(cell, LIVE_QUOTE_STATUSES)


def is_owed_invoice(cell: str) -> str:
    """Money that is still yours and not yet in the bank."""
    return in_list(cell, OWED_INVOICE_STATUSES)


def is_paid_invoice(cell: str) -> str:
    return in_list(cell, PAID_INVOICE_STATUSES)


def is_live_contract(cell: str) -> str:
    return in_list(cell, LIVE_CONTRACT_STATUSES)


def is_active_customer(cell: str) -> str:
    return in_list(cell, ACTIVE_CUSTOMER_STATUSES)


def is_usable_equipment(cell: str) -> str:
    return in_list(cell, USABLE_EQUIPMENT_STATUSES)


def is_job_cost(cell: str) -> str:
    """An expense that belongs to a job, not to the business."""
    return in_list(cell, JOB_COST_CATEGORIES)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Roll-ups across the registers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def sum_by(sheet: str, value_col: str, key_col: str, key_cell: str,
           *extra: str) -> str:
    """`SUMIFS` over one register, keyed on an ID.

    `extra` arrives in pairs - a column key and a criterion - because a
    SUMIFS criterion is always TWO arguments and writing it as one is
    the fastest way to a #VALUE! nobody can find.
    """
    parts = [f"[[{sheet}.{value_col}]]", f"[[{sheet}.{key_col}]]", key_cell]
    for index in range(0, len(extra), 2):
        parts.append(f"[[{sheet}.{extra[index]}]]")
        parts.append(extra[index + 1])
    return f"SUMIFS({','.join(parts)})"


def count_by(sheet: str, key_col: str, key_cell: str, *extra: str) -> str:
    parts = [f"[[{sheet}.{key_col}]]", key_cell]
    for index in range(0, len(extra), 2):
        parts.append(f"[[{sheet}.{extra[index]}]]")
        parts.append(extra[index + 1])
    return f"COUNTIFS({','.join(parts)})"


def jobs_done(key_col: str, key_cell: str) -> str:
    """Completed visits against a customer, property or service."""
    return count_by("Job & Work Orders", key_col, key_cell, "is_done", "1")


def revenue_from_jobs(key_col: str, key_cell: str) -> str:
    """What completed work was worth, before tax."""
    return sum_by("Job & Work Orders", "charge", key_col, key_cell,
                  "is_done", "1")


def labour_hours(job_cell: str) -> str:
    """Hours actually booked to a job on the timesheets."""
    return sum_by("Timesheets & Payroll", "hours", "job", job_cell)


def labour_cost(job_cell: str) -> str:
    """What those hours cost, at each person's own rate."""
    return sum_by("Timesheets & Payroll", "cost", "job", job_cell)


def material_cost(job_cell: str) -> str:
    """Materials booked out to a job, at cost."""
    return sum_by("Expense Tracker", "amount", "job", job_cell,
                  "is_job_cost", "1")


def invoiced_amount(job_cell: str) -> str:
    return sum_by("Invoice & Payments", "total", "job", job_cell)


def paid_amount(invoice_cell: str) -> str:
    return sum_by("Invoice & Payments", "paid", "id", invoice_cell)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The money
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def quote_price(area_cell: str, service_cell: str) -> str:
    """The catalogue price for a service at a given lawn area.

    Everything in the Service Catalog is priced per unit, and the unit
    varies - per visit, per hour, per 1,000 sq ft, per linear foot. The
    catalogue carries the rate and the unit; this works out which
    multiplier applies so one formula covers all thirty services.
    """
    rate = f'IFERROR(INDEX([[Service Catalog.rate]],MATCH({service_cell},[[Service Catalog.name]],0))*1,0)'
    unit = f'IFERROR(INDEX([[Service Catalog.unit]],MATCH({service_cell},[[Service Catalog.name]],0))&"","")'
    return (f'IF({service_cell}="",0,'
            f'ROUND({rate}*'
            f'IF({unit}="Per 1,000 sq ft",{area_cell}/1000,'
            f'IF({unit}="Per sq ft",{area_cell},'
            f'IF({unit}="Per 100 sq ft",{area_cell}/100,1)))'
            ',2))')


def service_minutes(area_cell: str, service_cell: str) -> str:
    """How long the catalogue says this service takes on this lawn."""
    mins = f'IFERROR(INDEX([[Service Catalog.minutes]],MATCH({service_cell},[[Service Catalog.name]],0))*1,0)'
    unit = f'IFERROR(INDEX([[Service Catalog.unit]],MATCH({service_cell},[[Service Catalog.name]],0))&"","")'
    return (f'IF({service_cell}="",0,'
            f'ROUND({mins}*'
            f'IF({unit}="Per 1,000 sq ft",{area_cell}/1000,'
            f'IF({unit}="Per sq ft",{area_cell},'
            f'IF({unit}="Per 100 sq ft",{area_cell}/100,1)))'
            ',0))')


def travel_cost(miles_cell: str) -> str:
    """What getting there costs the job."""
    return f'ROUND({miles_cell}*TravelRate,2)'


def overhead_cost(hours_cell: str) -> str:
    """The yard, the insurance and the admin, per crew hour.

    Leaving this out is how a job that looks profitable turns out not
    to be: a three-hour visit carries three hours of the business
    whether or not anybody thought about it.
    """
    return f'ROUND({hours_cell}*OverheadRate,2)'


def service_tax(amount: str) -> str:
    """Sales tax or VAT, only if the business is registered for it."""
    return f'IF(TaxOnServices<>"Yes",0,ROUND({amount}*TaxRate,2))'


def overtime_split(hours_cell: str) -> str:
    """Hours over the weekly threshold, which cost more."""
    return f'MAX(0,{hours_cell}-OvertimeAfter)'


def margin(part: str, whole: str) -> str:
    """A percentage that is blank rather than wrong when there is no base."""
    return f'IF({whole}<=0,"",ROUND({part}/{whole},4))'


def visits_per_year(frequency_cell: str) -> str:
    """Turn 'Fortnightly' into 26 - the parallel list does the work."""
    return ('IFERROR(INDEX(VisitsPerYear,'
            f'MATCH({frequency_cell},FrequencyList,0))*1,0)')


def days_between_visits(frequency_cell: str) -> str:
    return ('IFERROR(INDEX(DaysBetween,'
            f'MATCH({frequency_cell},FrequencyList,0))*1,0)')


def term_days(terms_cell: str) -> str:
    return f'IFERROR(INDEX(TermDays,MATCH({terms_cell},PaymentTermsList,0)),0)'


def season_of(date_cell: str) -> str:
    """Which season a date falls in, for the seasonal roll-ups."""
    return (f'IF({date_cell}="","",'
            f'IF(MONTH({date_cell})<=2,"Winter",'
            f'IF(MONTH({date_cell})<=5,"Spring",'
            f'IF(MONTH({date_cell})<=8,"Summer",'
            f'IF(MONTH({date_cell})<=11,"Autumn / Fall","Winter")))))')


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Alerts
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def alert_chain(trigger: str, tests, default: str = "OK") -> str:
    """Nested IFs from `(condition, message)` pairs, most urgent first.

    Nested rather than OR() or IFS(): OR() evaluates every argument
    even after one is already true, and IFS() needs a modern Excel.
    """
    body = f'"{default}"'
    for condition, message in reversed(tests):
        body = f'IF({condition},"{message}",{body})'
    return f'=IF({{{trigger}}}{{r}}="","",{body})'
````

### `31-landscaping/landscaping_spreadsheet/sheets/contracts.py`

<!-- source-file: 31-landscaping/landscaping_spreadsheet/sheets/contracts.py sha256:4d1ae3360f73f5de0f481fbb853507a81feae58411fa43957353dfc8ac9be017 -->
````python
"""10. Recurring Contracts - the income you can count on.

A contract says: this service, at this property, every so many days,
for this much. From that the sheet works out the next visit date, how
many visits are left this season, what the agreement is worth over a
year, and when it needs renewing.

The scheduler is deliberately a calculator, not a robot. It tells you
the next date a visit is due; you still create the job. A workbook
that silently invented rows would be a workbook you could not trust.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from ..config import Palette, Config
from ..layout import Col, SheetSpec
from ..sample_data import get as sample
from ..writer import date_check, list_from
from .common import (alert_cf, alert_chain, amount, count_by, customer_col,
                     date_num_col, id_col, is_live_contract,
                     lookup_customer, lookup_property, money_cf,
                     property_col, scale_cf, service_col, status_cf,
                     sum_by, yesno, zero)

NAME = "Recurring Contracts"


def spec(cfg: Config) -> SheetSpec:
    return SheetSpec(
        name=NAME,
        title="Recurring Contracts",
        subtitle="Standing agreements: what, where, how often, how "
                 "much, and when the next visit is due.",
        tab_color=Palette.primary_mid,
        rows=cfg.row_count("contracts"),
        samples=sample("contracts", cfg),
        freeze_cols=3,
        help_text=(
            "Set up one row per standing agreement. The next due date "
            "is worked out from the last completed visit and the "
            "frequency, so it moves on by itself as the work gets "
            "done. When a visit is due, create it on the Job & Work "
            "Orders tab and put this Contract ID on it."),
        extra_notes=[
            "This is a scheduling calculator, not an automatic "
            "booking system. It tells you what is due; you decide "
            "what actually gets booked, because weather, holidays and "
            "a broken mower all have a vote.",
            "Annual value is the honest measure of a contract. Twelve "
            "visits at $45 is a $540 customer, and that is the number "
            "to think about before offering a discount.",
            "Renewal reminders fire on the number of days set on "
            "Settings. Renewing a good contract is far cheaper than "
            "finding a new customer.",
        ],
        columns=[
            id_col("start_date", "ContractPrefix",
                   digits=cfg.digits("contract"), header="Contract ID",
                   note="Generated. Put it on every job that comes from "
                        "this agreement."),
            customer_col(),
            Col("customer_name", "Customer", 20, "text",
                formula=lookup_customer("name")),
            property_col(),
            Col("address", "Address", 26, "text",
                formula=lookup_property("address")),
            service_col(),
            Col("frequency", "Frequency", 16, "text",
                validate=list_from("FrequencyList"),
                note="How often the visit repeats. Drives both the next "
                     "due date and the annual value."),
            Col("day_pref", "Preferred day", 12, "text",
                validate=list_from("WeekdayList"),
                note="'Always Tuesdays' keeps a round tight and the "
                     "customer happy."),
            Col("start_date", "Starts", 11, "date",
                validate=date_check(),
                note="Start here. The row comes alive with a date."),
            Col("end_date", "Ends", 11, "date",
                validate=date_check(),
                note="Leave blank for a rolling agreement. Fill it in "
                     "for a fixed season."),
            Col("season_only", "Season only", 11, "flag",
                validate=yesno("Does this pause out of season?"),
                note="Mowing stops in winter; snow clearing does not. "
                     "The season months are on Settings."),
            Col("visit_price", "Price per visit", 12, "money",
                validate=amount(0, 1000000,
                                "What the customer pays for each "
                                "visit under this agreement."),
                note="The job register uses this automatically for "
                     "visits carrying this Contract ID."),
            Col("billing", "Billed", 16, "text",
                validate=list_from("PaymentTermsList"),
                note="How this one is invoiced - per visit, monthly in "
                     "advance, however you agreed it."),
            Col("po_number", "PO number", 14, "text",
                note="Commercial accounts often will not pay without "
                     "one."),
            Col("status", "Status", 13, "text",
                validate=list_from("ContractStatusList"),
                cf=status_cf()),
            Col("renewal_date", "Review on", 11, "date",
                validate=date_check(),
                note="When you will revisit the price. Put it in the "
                     "diary before the season starts, not during it."),
            Col("price_review", "Last price change", 13, "date",
                validate=date_check(),
                note="Two seasons without a change, with fuel and wages "
                     "where they are, is a quiet pay cut."),
            Col("notes", "Notes", 30, "wrap"),

            # ---- what it is worth ------------------------------------
            Col("visits_year", "Visits / year", 11, "int",
                formula=zero("start_date",
                             'IFERROR(INDEX(VisitsPerYear,'
                             'MATCH({frequency}{r},FrequencyList,0))*1,'
                             '0)'),
                note="From the frequency list on Settings."),
            Col("gap_days", "Days between", 11, "int",
                formula=zero("start_date",
                             'IFERROR(INDEX(DaysBetween,'
                             'MATCH({frequency}{r},FrequencyList,0))*1,'
                             '0)'),
                hidden=True),
            Col("annual_value", "Annual value", 12, "money",
                formula=zero("start_date",
                             'ROUND({visit_price}{r}*'
                             '{visits_year}{r},2)'),
                cf=money_cf(),
                note="Price per visit times visits per year. The number "
                     "that says how much this customer matters."),
            Col("monthly_value", "Per month", 11, "money",
                formula=zero("start_date",
                             'ROUND({annual_value}{r}/12,2)'),
                note="The same money spread evenly - useful when a "
                     "customer wants a flat monthly bill."),
            Col("visits_done", "Visits done", 11, "int",
                formula=zero("start_date", count_by("Job & Work Orders",
                                                    "contract", '{id}{r}',
                                                    "is_done", "1")),
                cf=scale_cf()),
            Col("visits_booked", "Visits booked", 12, "int",
                formula=zero("start_date", count_by("Job & Work Orders",
                                                    "contract",
                                                    '{id}{r}',
                                                    "is_open", "1"))),
            Col("revenue", "Revenue to date", 13, "money",
                formula=zero("start_date", sum_by("Job & Work Orders",
                                                  "charge", "contract",
                                                  '{id}{r}',
                                                  "is_done", "1")),
                cf=money_cf()),
            Col("cost_total", "Cost to date", 12, "money",
                formula=zero("start_date", sum_by("Job & Work Orders",
                                                  "cost", "contract",
                                                  '{id}{r}',
                                                  "is_done", "1"))),
            Col("profit", "Profit to date", 13, "money",
                formula=zero("start_date",
                             'ROUND({revenue}{r}-{cost_total}{r},2)'),
                cf=[{"type": "cell", "criteria": "<", "value": 0,
                     "fmt": "bold_bad"},
                    {"type": "cell", "criteria": ">", "value": 0,
                     "fmt": "good"}]),
            Col("margin_pct", "Margin", 9, "percent",
                formula='=IF({start_date}{r}="","",'
                        'IF({revenue}{r}<=0,"",'
                        'ROUND({profit}{r}/{revenue}{r},4)))',
                cf=[{"type": "cell", "criteria": ">=",
                     "value": "=TargetMargin", "fmt": "good"},
                    {"type": "cell", "criteria": "<",
                     "value": "=MinMargin", "fmt": "bad"}],
                note="A contract below your floor is one to renegotiate "
                     "at review, not to cancel in a temper."),

            # ---- when the next one is due ----------------------------
            Col("last_num", "Last visit #", 11, "number",
                formula=zero("start_date",
                             'SUMPRODUCT(MAX('
                             '([[Job & Work Orders.contract]]={id}{r})*'
                             '([[Job & Work Orders.is_done]]=1)*'
                             '[[Job & Work Orders.date_num]]))'),
                hidden=True),
            Col("last_visit", "Last visit", 11, "date",
                formula='=IF({start_date}{r}="","",'
                        'IF({last_num}{r}<=0,"",{last_num}{r}))'),
            Col("next_num", "Next due #", 10, "number",
                formula=zero("start_date",
                             'IF({is_live}{r}=0,0,'
                             'IF({gap_days}{r}<=0,0,'
                             'IF({last_num}{r}<=0,{start_date}{r},'
                             '{last_num}{r}+{gap_days}{r})))'),
                hidden=True),
            Col("next_due", "Next due", 11, "date",
                formula='=IF({start_date}{r}="","",'
                        'IF({next_num}{r}<=0,"",'
                        '{next_num}{r}))',
                cf=[{"type": "formula",
                     "criteria": '=AND(ISNUMBER({next_due}{r}),'
                                 '{next_due}{r}<TodayDate)',
                     "fmt": "bad"}],
                note="Last completed visit plus the gap, or the start "
                     "date if nothing has happened yet."),
            Col("days_to_next", "Days to next", 11, "int",
                formula=zero("start_date",
                             'IF({next_num}{r}<=0,0,'
                             '{next_num}{r}-TodayDate)'),
                cf=[{"type": "cell", "criteria": "<", "value": 0,
                     "fmt": "bad"},
                    {"type": "cell", "criteria": "<=", "value": 7,
                     "fmt": "warn"}],
                note="Negative means the visit is already late."),
            Col("booked_next", "Next booked", 7, "int",
                formula=zero("start_date",
                             'COUNTIFS([[Job & Work Orders.contract]],'
                             '{id}{r},[[Job & Work Orders.is_open]],1)'),
                hidden=True),
            Col("days_to_renew", "Days to review", 12, "int",
                formula=zero("start_date",
                             'IF({renewal_date}{r}="",0,'
                             '{renewal_date}{r}-TodayDate)'),
                cf=[{"type": "cell", "criteria": "<", "value": 0,
                     "fmt": "bad"},
                    {"type": "cell", "criteria": "<=",
                     "value": "=RenewalWarnDays", "fmt": "warn"}]),
            Col("days_to_end", "Days to end", 11, "int",
                formula=zero("start_date",
                             'IF({end_date}{r}="",9999,'
                             '{end_date}{r}-TodayDate)'),
                hidden=True),
            Col("is_live", "Live", 6, "int",
                formula=zero("start_date",
                             f'IF(AND({is_live_contract("{status}{r}")},'
                             '({end_date}{r}="")+'
                             '({end_date}{r}>=TodayDate)>0),1,0)'),
                hidden=True),
            Col("is_due", "Due", 6, "int",
                formula=zero("start_date",
                             'IF(AND({is_live}{r}=1,{next_num}{r}>0,'
                             '{next_num}{r}<=TodayDate+UpcomingDays,'
                             '{booked_next}{r}=0),1,0)'),
                hidden=True),
            date_num_col("next_due", "next_date_num", header="Next #"),

            Col("alert", "What needs doing", 46, "wrap",
                formula=alert_chain("start_date", [
                    ('AND({is_live}{r}=1,{days_to_next}{r}<0,'
                     '{booked_next}{r}=0)',
                     "Overdue - a visit is past due and nothing is "
                     "booked"),
                    ('AND({is_live}{r}=1,{visit_price}{r}=0)',
                     "Add - no price agreed, so the visits earn nothing"),
                    ('AND({is_live}{r}=1,{days_to_renew}{r}<0,'
                     '{renewal_date}{r}<>"")',
                     "Renew - the review date has passed"),
                    ('AND({is_live}{r}=1,{renewal_date}{r}<>"",'
                     '{days_to_renew}{r}<=RenewalWarnDays)',
                     "Renew - review date coming up, agree the new "
                     "price"),
                    ('AND({is_live}{r}=1,{end_date}{r}<>"",'
                     '{days_to_end}{r}<=RenewalWarnDays,'
                     '{days_to_end}{r}>=0)',
                     "Renew - this agreement ends soon"),
                    ('AND({revenue}{r}>0,{profit}{r}<0)',
                     "Loss - this contract is costing you money"),
                    ('{is_due}{r}=1',
                     "Schedule - next visit due, create the work order"),
                    ('AND({is_live}{r}=1,{margin_pct}{r}<>"",'
                     '{margin_pct}{r}<MinMargin)',
                     "Thin margin - raise it at the next review"),
                    ('AND({is_live}{r}=1,{price_review}{r}<>"",'
                     'TodayDate-{price_review}{r}>730)',
                     "Check - the price has not changed in two years"),
                    ('AND({is_live}{r}=1,{renewal_date}{r}="")',
                     "Add - no review date set"),
                ]),
                cf=alert_cf()),
        ],
    )
````

### `31-landscaping/landscaping_spreadsheet/sheets/crew.py`

<!-- source-file: 31-landscaping/landscaping_spreadsheet/sheets/crew.py sha256:73a13289078b7a5e2dcbd5c3dddcb87a796b347ed0e440bb0e709a8977832f03 -->
````python
"""11. Crew Database - the people, their rates and their paperwork.

The hourly cost recorded here is what the whole workbook uses to work
out what a job cost. It should be the loaded cost - wage plus payroll
tax plus insurance plus the share of the truck they ride in - not the
figure on their payslip. If you put the payslip number in, every job
in the workbook will look more profitable than it is.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from ..config import ACTIVE_CREW_STATUSES, Palette, Config
from ..layout import Col, SheetSpec
from ..sample_data import get as sample
from ..writer import date_check, list_from
from .common import (alert_cf, alert_chain, amount, count_by, id_col,
                     in_list, money_cf, rank_desc, rating_cf, scale_cf,
                     status_cf, sum_by, yesno, zero)

NAME = "Crew Database"


def spec(cfg: Config) -> SheetSpec:
    return SheetSpec(
        name=NAME,
        title="Crew Database",
        subtitle="Who works for you, what they cost per hour, what "
                 "they are qualified to do and when it expires.",
        tab_color=Palette.primary_mid,
        rows=cfg.row_count("crew"),
        samples=sample("crew", cfg),
        help_text=(
            "Add each person once. The Employee ID appears "
            "automatically and feeds the timesheets, where hours are "
            "costed at that person's own rate. Expiry dates for "
            "licences and certificates are tracked here and warn you "
            "before they lapse."),
        extra_notes=[
            "Hourly cost should be the loaded cost, not the wage. A "
            "$20 wage usually costs the business $26 to $30 once tax, "
            "insurance and downtime are counted. Guessing low here "
            "makes every job in the workbook look better than it is.",
            "Keep people who have left, with status 'Left'. Their "
            "hours are part of last season's costs, and deleting the "
            "row leaves those timesheets pointing at nobody.",
            "This is a record of hours and rates for your own "
            "planning. It is not a payroll system and it does not "
            "calculate tax withholding - your payroll provider or "
            "accountant does that.",
        ],
        columns=[
            id_col("name", "CrewPrefix", digits=cfg.digits("crew"),
                   header="Employee ID",
                   note="Generated. The timesheets point at this."),
            Col("name", "Name", 22, "text",
                note="Start here."),
            Col("role", "Role", 20, "text",
                validate=list_from("CrewRoleList")),
            Col("crew", "Usual crew", 12, "text",
                validate=list_from("CrewNameList"),
                note="Which truck they normally ride with."),
            Col("employment", "Employment", 16, "text",
                validate=list_from("EmploymentTypeList"),
                note="Seasonal and subcontract people cost differently "
                     "and are worth separating."),
            Col("phone", "Phone", 15, "text"),
            Col("email", "Email", 24, "text"),
            Col("emergency", "Emergency contact", 22, "text",
                note="Name and number. The one field you hope never to "
                     "use, and must have when you do."),
            Col("start_date", "Started", 11, "date",
                validate=date_check()),
            Col("end_date", "Left", 11, "date",
                validate=date_check(),
                note="Fill in rather than deleting the row."),
            Col("status", "Status", 12, "text",
                validate=list_from("CrewStatusList"),
                cf=status_cf()),
            Col("pay_rate", "Pay rate / hr", 12, "money",
                validate=amount(0, 1000, "What you pay them per hour."),
                note="The wage itself, for reference and for payroll."),
            Col("cost_rate", "Cost to you / hr", 13, "money",
                validate=amount(0, 1000,
                                "Wage plus payroll tax plus insurance "
                                "plus overheads attached to this "
                                "person."),
                note="The real number. This is what costs every job in "
                     "the workbook. Blank falls back to the crew rate "
                     "on Settings."),
            Col("overtime_rate", "Overtime x", 10, "number1",
                validate=amount(1, 5,
                                "Multiplier for hours over the weekly "
                                "threshold."),
                note="Blank uses the multiplier on Settings."),
            Col("licence", "Licence / cert", 20, "text",
                note="Pesticide applicator, chainsaw ticket, CDL. The "
                     "ones that stop work if they lapse."),
            Col("licence_expiry", "Expires", 11, "date",
                validate=date_check(),
                cf=[{"type": "formula",
                     "criteria": '=AND(ISNUMBER({licence_expiry}{r}),'
                                 '{licence_expiry}{r}<TodayDate)',
                     "fmt": "bold_bad"}],
                note="Warned about well before the date, and in red "
                     "after it."),
            Col("insurance_expiry", "Insurance to", 12, "date",
                validate=date_check()),
            Col("licence_days", "Days to expiry", 12, "int",
                formula=zero("name",
                             'IF({licence_expiry}{r}="",9999,'
                             '{licence_expiry}{r}-TodayDate)'),
                hidden=True),
            Col("can_spray", "Can spray", 10, "flag",
                validate=yesno("Are they licensed to apply pesticide or "
                               "fertiliser?"),
                note="Jobs flagged as needing a licence should only go "
                     "to people marked Yes here."),
            Col("can_drive", "Can drive", 10, "flag",
                validate=yesno()),
            Col("equipment_ok", "Machinery trained", 14, "wrap",
                note="Which machines they are signed off on. A free "
                     "text note, because every yard is different."),
            Col("notes", "Notes", 28, "wrap"),

            # ---- what they actually do -------------------------------
            Col("hours_total", "Hours logged", 12, "number1",
                formula=zero("name", sum_by("Timesheets & Payroll",
                                            "hours", "employee",
                                            '{id}{r}')),
                cf=scale_cf()),
            Col("hours_year", "Hours this year", 13, "number1",
                formula=zero("name", sum_by(
                    "Timesheets & Payroll", "hours", "employee",
                    '{id}{r}',
                    "date_num", '">="&YearStart',
                    "date_num", '"<="&YearEnd'))),
            Col("hours_billable", "Billable hours", 13, "number1",
                formula=zero("name", sum_by("Timesheets & Payroll",
                                            "hours", "employee",
                                            '{id}{r}',
                                            "is_billable", "1")),
                note="Hours booked to a job, as opposed to travel, "
                     "yard time and machine repairs."),
            Col("billable_pct", "Billable %", 10, "percent",
                formula='=IF({name}{r}="","",'
                        'IF({hours_total}{r}<=0,"",'
                        'ROUND({hours_billable}{r}/'
                        '{hours_total}{r},4)))',
                cf=[{"type": "cell", "criteria": ">=", "value": 0.75,
                     "fmt": "good"},
                    {"type": "cell", "criteria": "<", "value": 0.5,
                     "fmt": "bad"}],
                note="The number that explains a bad month better than "
                     "anything else. Below 60% means the day is being "
                     "eaten by driving and faffing."),
            Col("cost_total", "Labour cost", 12, "money",
                formula=zero("name", sum_by("Timesheets & Payroll",
                                            "cost", "employee",
                                            '{id}{r}'))),
            Col("revenue", "Revenue worked on", 15, "money",
                formula=zero("name", sum_by("Timesheets & Payroll",
                                            "job_value", "employee",
                                            '{id}{r}')),
                cf=money_cf(),
                note="Their share of what the jobs they worked on were "
                     "worth. A rough measure, but a fair one."),
            Col("value_per_hour", "Value per hour", 13, "money",
                formula='=IF({name}{r}="","",'
                        'IF({hours_billable}{r}<=0,"",'
                        'ROUND({revenue}{r}/'
                        '{hours_billable}{r},2)))',
                cf=[{"type": "cell", "criteria": ">=",
                     "value": "=ChargeRate", "fmt": "good"},
                    {"type": "cell", "criteria": "<",
                     "value": "=ChargeRate", "fmt": "warn"}]),
            Col("jobs_done", "Jobs worked", 11, "int",
                formula=zero("name", count_by("Timesheets & Payroll",
                                              "employee", '{id}{r}',
                                              "is_billable", "1"))),
            Col("rating", "Quality score", 12, "number1",
                formula='=IF({name}{r}="","",'
                        'IFERROR(AVERAGEIFS('
                        '[[Customer Feedback.score]],'
                        '[[Customer Feedback.crew]],{crew}{r},'
                        '[[Customer Feedback.score]],">0"),""))',
                cf=rating_cf(),
                note="Feedback for the crew they ride with, since "
                     "customers rate the visit, not the individual."),
            Col("overtime_hours", "Overtime hrs", 11, "number1",
                formula=zero("name", sum_by("Timesheets & Payroll",
                                            "overtime_hours", "employee",
                                            '{id}{r}')),
                cf=[{"type": "cell", "criteria": ">", "value": 0,
                     "fmt": "warn"}]),
            Col("is_active", "Active", 7, "int",
                formula=zero("name",
                             f'IF({in_list("{status}{r}", ACTIVE_CREW_STATUSES)},'
                             '1,0)'),
                hidden=True),
            rank_desc("revenue", guard='{name}{r}=""'),

            Col("alert", "What needs doing", 44, "wrap",
                formula=alert_chain("name", [
                    ('AND({is_active}{r}=1,{licence}{r}<>"",'
                     '{licence_days}{r}<0)',
                     "Expired - licence has lapsed, they cannot do "
                     "that work"),
                    ('AND({is_active}{r}=1,{cost_rate}{r}=0,'
                     '{pay_rate}{r}=0)',
                     "Add - no rate set, so their hours cost nothing"),
                    ('AND({is_active}{r}=1,{licence}{r}<>"",'
                     '{licence_days}{r}<=60)',
                     "Renew - licence expires within two months"),
                    ('AND({is_active}{r}=1,{emergency}{r}="")',
                     "Add - no emergency contact on file"),
                    ('{overtime_hours}{r}>0',
                     "Check - overtime logged, is the round too big?"),
                    ('AND({hours_total}{r}>0,{billable_pct}{r}<>"",'
                     '{billable_pct}{r}<0.5)',
                     "Check - under half their hours are billable"),
                    ('AND({is_active}{r}=1,{hours_total}{r}=0)',
                     "Action - no hours ever logged for this person"),
                    ('AND({is_active}{r}=1,{cost_rate}{r}=0)',
                     "Add - no loaded cost rate, jobs use the default"),
                ]),
                cf=alert_cf()),
        ],
    )
````

### `31-landscaping/landscaping_spreadsheet/sheets/customers.py`

<!-- source-file: 31-landscaping/landscaping_spreadsheet/sheets/customers.py sha256:588627ba2b16277844700493e4952871cb958cbc4a763c73fdb5eaf10e0f32c4 -->
````python
"""4. Customer CRM - everybody who pays you, and what they are worth.

The Customer ID generated here is the first of the four join keys. A
property belongs to a customer, a job happens at a property, and an
invoice bills a customer for jobs. Get this ID wrong and the chain
comes apart three tabs later with nothing to say why.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from ..config import Palette, Config
from ..layout import Col, SheetSpec
from ..sample_data import get as sample
from ..writer import date_check, list_from
from .common import (alert_cf, alert_chain, count_by, id_col,
                     is_active_customer, loss_cf, margin, money_cf,
                     owing_cf, rank_desc, rating_cf, scale_cf, status_cf,
                     sum_by, yesno, zero)

NAME = "Customer CRM"


def spec(cfg: Config) -> SheetSpec:
    rows = cfg.row_count("customers")
    return SheetSpec(
        name=NAME,
        title="Customer CRM",
        subtitle="Everyone who pays you, what they have spent, and who "
                 "has gone quiet. One row per customer, never per visit.",
        tab_color=Palette.primary,
        rows=rows,
        samples=sample("customers", cfg),
        help_text=(
            "Add the customer here first. The Customer ID appears "
            "automatically and becomes available in every drop-down "
            "that needs it - properties, quotes, jobs, invoices. "
            "A household with two addresses is ONE customer with two "
            "properties, not two customers."),
        extra_notes=[
            "Lifetime value counts completed jobs only, so a quote "
            "nobody accepted never inflates what somebody looks worth.",
            "'Dormant' is worked out, not typed: it is how long since "
            "their last completed visit against the window on Settings.",
        ],
        columns=[
            id_col("name", "CustomerPrefix", digits=cfg.digits("customer"),
                   header="Customer ID",
                   note="Generated. This is the join key - every property, "
                        "job and invoice points back at it."),
            Col("name", "Customer name", 24, "text",
                note="A household, a company or a managing agent. Start "
                     "typing here and the row comes alive."),
            Col("contact", "Main contact", 18, "text",
                note="Who you actually speak to."),
            Col("phone", "Phone", 15, "text"),
            Col("email", "Email", 26, "text"),
            Col("address", "Billing address", 30, "wrap",
                note="Where the invoice goes. The place you mow is a "
                     "Property, on the next tab."),
            Col("town", "Town / city", 16, "text"),
            Col("postcode", "Zip / postcode", 12, "text"),
            Col("type", "Customer type", 20, "text",
                validate=list_from("CustomerTypeList"),
                note="Commercial work pays later and in bigger lumps. "
                     "Worth being able to split the two."),
            Col("source", "How they found you", 20, "text",
                validate=list_from("LeadSourceList"),
                note="Fill this in for a year and you will stop paying "
                     "for the adverts that do not work."),
            Col("first_job", "Customer since", 13, "date",
                validate=date_check()),
            Col("terms", "Payment terms", 17, "text",
                validate=list_from("PaymentTermsList"),
                note="Drives the due date on every invoice to them."),
            Col("method", "Pays by", 16, "text",
                validate=list_from("PaymentMethodList")),
            Col("status", "Status", 13, "text",
                validate=list_from("CustomerStatusList"),
                cf=status_cf()),
            Col("rating", "You rate them", 11, "rating",
                validate={"validate": "integer", "criteria": "between",
                          "minimum": 1, "maximum": 5,
                          "error_title": "1 to 5",
                          "error_message": "How good are they to work "
                                           "for? 5 is a dream job, 1 is "
                                           "one you dread."},
                cf=rating_cf(),
                note="Pays on time, dog is friendly, gate is unlocked. "
                     "Your own judgement, for your own planning."),
            Col("po_required", "Needs a PO", 10, "flag",
                validate=yesno("Does this customer require a purchase "
                               "order number before you can invoice?"),
                note="Commercial accounts often do, and an invoice "
                     "without one does not get paid."),
            Col("tax_exempt", "Tax exempt", 10, "flag",
                validate=yesno()),
            Col("marketing_ok", "Marketing OK", 11, "flag",
                validate=yesno("Have they agreed to seasonal offers and "
                               "reminders?"),
                note="Ask once, record it, and respect it."),
            Col("notes", "Notes", 34, "wrap",
                note="The things that are not a field: 'ring the bell, "
                     "do not use the side gate', 'always wants the "
                     "clippings left'."),

            # ---- what they are actually worth ------------------------
            Col("properties", "Properties", 10, "int",
                formula=zero("name", count_by("Property Database",
                                              "customer", '{id}{r}')),
                note="Automatic. How many addresses you look after for "
                     "them."),
            Col("jobs_done", "Visits done", 11, "int",
                formula=zero("name", count_by("Job & Work Orders",
                                              "customer", '{id}{r}',
                                              "is_done", "1")),
                cf=scale_cf()),
            Col("jobs_open", "Visits booked", 12, "int",
                formula=zero("name", count_by("Job & Work Orders",
                                              "customer", '{id}{r}',
                                              "is_open", "1"))),
            Col("lifetime", "Lifetime revenue", 15, "money",
                formula=zero("name", sum_by("Job & Work Orders", "charge",
                                            "customer", '{id}{r}',
                                            "is_done", "1")),
                cf=money_cf(),
                note="Completed work only. This is the number that tells "
                     "you who you cannot afford to lose."),
            Col("revenue_year", "This year", 13, "money",
                formula=zero("name", sum_by(
                    "Job & Work Orders", "charge", "customer", '{id}{r}',
                    "is_done", "1",
                    "date_num", '">="&YearStart',
                    "date_num", '"<="&YearEnd')),
                cf=money_cf()),
            Col("cost_total", "Cost to serve", 13, "money",
                formula=zero("name", sum_by("Job & Work Orders", "cost",
                                            "customer", '{id}{r}',
                                            "is_done", "1"))),
            Col("profit", "Profit", 12, "money",
                formula=zero("name", 'ROUND({lifetime}{r}-'
                                     '{cost_total}{r},2)'),
                cf=loss_cf(),
                note="What they have actually left you with after the "
                     "crew, the materials and the drive."),
            Col("margin_pct", "Margin", 9, "percent",
                formula='=IF({name}{r}="","",'
                        f'{margin("{profit}{r}", "{lifetime}{r}")})',
                cf=scale_cf()),
            Col("avg_job", "Average visit", 13, "money",
                formula='=IF({name}{r}="","",'
                        'IF({jobs_done}{r}<=0,"",'
                        'ROUND({lifetime}{r}/{jobs_done}{r},2)))'),
            Col("contracts", "Contracts", 10, "int",
                formula=zero("name", count_by("Recurring Contracts",
                                              "customer", '{id}{r}',
                                              "is_live", "1")),
                note="Live recurring agreements. A customer with one is "
                     "worth far more than one without."),
            Col("contract_value", "Contract / yr", 13, "money",
                formula=zero("name", sum_by("Recurring Contracts",
                                            "annual_value", "customer",
                                            '{id}{r}', "is_live", "1")),
                cf=money_cf(),
                note="Booked recurring income. The number a buyer of "
                     "your business would look at first."),

            # ---- money owed ------------------------------------------
            Col("invoiced", "Invoiced", 12, "money",
                formula=zero("name", sum_by("Invoice & Payments", "total",
                                            "customer", '{id}{r}'))),
            Col("received", "Received", 12, "money",
                formula=zero("name", sum_by("Invoice & Payments", "paid",
                                            "customer", '{id}{r}'))),
            Col("owing", "Owing", 11, "money",
                formula=zero("name", 'ROUND({invoiced}{r}-'
                                     '{received}{r},2)'),
                cf=owing_cf()),
            Col("overdue", "Overdue", 11, "money",
                formula=zero("name", sum_by("Invoice & Payments",
                                            "outstanding", "customer",
                                            '{id}{r}', "is_overdue", "1")),
                cf=owing_cf(),
                note="Past the due date and still unpaid. Chase this "
                     "column before you chase anything else."),
            Col("oldest_due", "Days late", 10, "int",
                formula=zero("name", 'IF({overdue}{r}<=0,0,'
                                     'MAX(0,SUMPRODUCT(MAX('
                                     '([[Invoice & Payments.customer]]='
                                     '{id}{r})*'
                                     '[[Invoice & Payments.days_late]]))))'),
                cf=[{"type": "cell", "criteria": ">=", "value": 30,
                     "fmt": "bold_bad"},
                    {"type": "cell", "criteria": ">", "value": 0,
                     "fmt": "warn"}],
                note="The worst one, not the average. A single 90 day "
                     "debt is a different conversation."),

            # ---- how they are getting on -----------------------------
            Col("last_job_num", "Last visit #", 11, "number",
                formula=zero("name", 'SUMPRODUCT(MAX('
                                     '([[Job & Work Orders.customer]]='
                                     '{id}{r})*'
                                     '([[Job & Work Orders.is_done]]=1)*'
                                     '[[Job & Work Orders.date_num]]))'),
                hidden=True),
            Col("last_job", "Last visit", 12, "date",
                formula='=IF({name}{r}="","",'
                        'IF({last_job_num}{r}<=0,"",'
                        '{last_job_num}{r}))',
                note="Automatic, from the job register."),
            Col("days_since", "Days since", 10, "int",
                formula=zero("name", 'IF({last_job_num}{r}<=0,0,'
                                     'TodayDate-{last_job_num}{r})'),
                cf=[{"type": "cell", "criteria": ">=",
                     "value": "=DormantDays", "fmt": "bad"}]),
            Col("rating_given", "Their rating", 11, "number1",
                formula='=IF({name}{r}="","",'
                        'IFERROR(AVERAGEIFS('
                        '[[Customer Feedback.score]],'
                        '[[Customer Feedback.customer]],{id}{r},'
                        '[[Customer Feedback.score]],">0"),""))',
                cf=rating_cf(),
                note="What they think of you, averaged from the feedback "
                     "tab. The other direction to the column above."),
            Col("complaints", "Complaints", 10, "int",
                formula=zero("name", count_by("Customer Feedback",
                                              "customer", '{id}{r}',
                                              "is_problem", "1")),
                cf=[{"type": "cell", "criteria": ">=", "value": 2,
                     "fmt": "bad"},
                    {"type": "cell", "criteria": ">", "value": 0,
                     "fmt": "warn"}]),
            Col("is_active", "Active", 7, "int",
                formula=zero("name", f'IF({is_active_customer("{status}{r}")},'
                                     '1,0)'),
                hidden=True),
            rank_desc("lifetime", guard='{name}{r}=""',
                      note="1 = your most valuable customer. The "
                           "dashboard reads this to list them."),
            Col("alert", "What needs doing", 46, "wrap",
                formula=alert_chain("name", [
                    ('{overdue}{r}>0',
                     "Overdue - invoice past its due date, chase it"),
                    ('{complaints}{r}>=2',
                     "Urgent - more than one complaint logged, call them"),
                    ('AND({status}{r}="Lead",{jobs_done}{r}=0)',
                     "Follow up - a lead with no work done yet"),
                    ('{properties}{r}=0',
                     "Add - no property on file, so nothing can be booked"),
                    ('AND({is_active}{r}=1,{days_since}{r}>=DormantDays,'
                     '{jobs_open}{r}=0)',
                     "Dormant - no visit for a long time and nothing "
                     "booked"),
                    ('AND({contracts}{r}=0,{jobs_done}{r}>=4)',
                     "Action - a regular customer with no contract, ask "
                     "for one"),
                    ('AND({lifetime}{r}>0,{margin_pct}{r}<>"",'
                     '{margin_pct}{r}<MinMargin)',
                     "Thin margin - this customer earns less than your "
                     "floor"),
                    ('{owing}{r}>0', "Due - invoiced and not yet paid"),
                    ('{email}{r}=""', "Add - no email address on file"),
                    ('{terms}{r}=""', "Add - payment terms not set"),
                ]),
                cf=alert_cf()),
        ],
    )
````

### `31-landscaping/landscaping_spreadsheet/sheets/dashboard.py`

<!-- source-file: 31-landscaping/landscaping_spreadsheet/sheets/dashboard.py sha256:c3850f313cc9bb169def31dbc9c44af01f057f8e519f6ce5ecc35eadc8bf939f -->
````python
"""`Dashboard` - the page that answers "what do I need to do today?"

Everything here is worked out from the other tabs, so nothing is ever
out of date and there is nothing to refresh. The questions are in the
order somebody running a lawn care round actually asks them: what is
on today, what has slipped, who owes me money, what is about to break,
and is any of this actually making a profit.

The top strip is deliberately the week rather than the year. A
landscaping business is run a week at a time; the year is something
you look at in January.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from ..config import Config, Palette
from ..layout import Registry
from ..writer import SheetWriter

NAME = "Dashboard"
LAST_COL = 12
LIST_ROWS = 8


def _alert_count(sheet: str, prefix: str) -> str:
    """How many rows on a register are shouting a given prefix."""
    return f'COUNTIF([[{sheet}.alert]],"{prefix}*")'


#: every register that carries a "What needs doing" column
ALERT_SHEETS = [
    "Customer CRM", "Property Database", "Service Catalog",
    "Quote Calculator", "Job & Work Orders", "Recurring Contracts",
    "Crew Database", "Crew Schedule", "Timesheets & Payroll",
    "Equipment Inventory", "Vehicle & Fuel Tracker",
    "Materials Inventory", "Invoice & Payments", "Expense Tracker",
    "Customer Feedback", "Profit Analysis",
]


def _all_alerts(prefix: str) -> str:
    """Total rows across the workbook whose alert starts with prefix."""
    return "+".join(_alert_count(sheet, prefix)
                    for sheet in ALERT_SHEETS)


def _by_rank(sheet: str, rank_key: str, field: str, n: int) -> str:
    """The nth row of a register by one of its hidden rank columns."""
    return (f'IFERROR(INDEX([[{sheet}.{field}]],MATCH({n},'
            f'[[{sheet}.{rank_key}]],0)),"")')


def build(book, fmts, cfg: Config, reg: Registry) -> SheetWriter:
    s = SheetWriter(book, fmts, cfg, reg, NAME, tab_color=Palette.deep)

    s.banner("Landscaping Business Dashboard",
             "Today, this week, the money and the machines - worked "
             "out from the tabs you have already filled in.",
             LAST_COL)
    s.set_col(0, 0, 26)
    for column in range(1, LAST_COL + 1):
        s.set_col(column, column, 13)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------ head --
    row = 4
    s.merge(row, 0, 0, "Business", fmts.chrome("label_bold"))
    s.merge(row, 1, 3, None, fmts.calc("text"))
    s.formula(row, 1, "=BusinessName", fmts.calc("text"))
    s.merge(row, 4, 4, "Today", fmts.chrome("label_right"))
    s.formula(row, 5, "=TodayDate", fmts.calc("date"))
    s.merge(row, 6, 6, "Customers", fmts.chrome("label_right"))
    s.formula(row, 7, "=SUM(CustIsActive)", fmts.calc("int"))
    s.merge(row, 8, 8, "Properties", fmts.chrome("label_right"))
    s.formula(row, 9, "=SUM(PropIsActive)", fmts.calc("int"))
    s.merge(row, 10, LAST_COL, None, fmts.chrome("note"))
    s.formula(
        row, 10,
        '="Figures update the moment you type. Nothing to refresh."',
        fmts.chrome("note"))
    row += 2

    # -------------------------------------------------------- the week --
    row = s.section(row, "Today and the week ahead", LAST_COL)
    s.kpi(row, 0, "Jobs today", "=SUM(JobIsToday)", "int",
          note="Booked for today and not yet closed off")
    s.kpi(row, 2, "Jobs this week", "=SUM(JobIsWeek)", "int",
          note="Within the upcoming window on Settings")
    s.kpi(row, 4, "Hours booked",
          '=SUMIFS(JobHoursEst,JobIsOpen,1,JobDateNum,'
          '">="&TodayDate,JobDateNum,"<="&TodayDate+UpcomingDays)',
          "number1", note="Crew hours the week needs")
    s.kpi(row, 6, "Worth this week",
          '=SUMIFS(JobCharge,JobIsOpen,1,JobDateNum,">="&TodayDate,'
          'JobDateNum,"<="&TodayDate+UpcomingDays)', "money",
          note="Value of what is booked")
    s.kpi(row, 8, "Unassigned",
          '=COUNTIFS(JobIsOpen,1,JobCrew,"Unassigned")', "int",
          note="Booked with nobody to do it")
    row = s.kpi(row, 10, "Behind schedule",
                '=COUNTIFS(JobIsOpen,1,JobDateNum,"<"&TodayDate)',
                "int", span=3,
                note="Past their date and still open")
    row += 1

    # ------------------------------------------------- work that slipped --
    row = s.section(row, "Work you still owe", LAST_COL)
    row = s.note(
        row,
        "Rain, breakdowns and locked gates are part of the trade. "
        "What costs money is forgetting about them. Everything in "
        "this row is work that was promised and has not happened.",
        LAST_COL, height=30)
    row += 1
    s.kpi(row, 0, "Rained off / revisit", "=SUM(JobIsCatchup)", "int",
          note="Waiting to be rescheduled")
    s.kpi(row, 2, "Contract visits due", "=SUM(ConIsDue)", "int",
          note="Due by the contract and not booked")
    s.kpi(row, 4, "Quotes waiting",
          f"={_alert_count('Quote Calculator', 'Chase -')}", "int",
          note="Sent, no answer, past the chase window")
    s.kpi(row, 6, "Quotes to convert",
          f"={_alert_count('Quote Calculator', 'Action -')}", "int",
          note="Accepted with no work order raised")
    s.kpi(row, 8, "Completed, unbilled", "=SUM(JobIsUnbilled)", "int",
          note="Done and never invoiced")
    row = s.kpi(row, 10, "Value unbilled",
                "=SUMPRODUCT(JobIsUnbilled*JobCharge)", "money",
                span=3, note="Money sitting on the job sheet")
    row += 1

    # ------------------------------------------------------- the money --
    row = s.section(row, "The money", LAST_COL)
    s.kpi(row, 0, "Owed to you", "=SUM(InvOutstanding)", "money",
          note="Invoiced and not yet paid")
    s.kpi(row, 2, "Overdue", "=SUMPRODUCT(InvIsOverdue*InvOutstanding)",
          "money", note="Past the due date - chase these")
    s.kpi(row, 4, "Over 60 days",
          '=SUMIFS(InvOutstanding,InvDaysLate,">=60")', "money",
          note="The ones that need a decision")
    s.kpi(row, 6, "Revenue this month",
          "=SUMIFS(JobCharge,JobMonth,ThisMonthKey,JobIsDone,1)",
          "money", note="Completed visits, excluding tax")
    s.kpi(row, 8, "Costs this month",
          '=SUMIFS(ExpPeriodCost,ExpMonth,ThisMonthKey)+'
          'SUMIFS(TimeCost,TimeMonth,ThisMonthKey)+'
          'SUMIFS(JobLabourFallback,JobMonth,ThisMonthKey)+'
          'SUMIFS(VehAmount,VehMonth,ThisMonthKey)', "money",
          note="Labour, expenses and vehicles")
    row = s.kpi(row, 10, "Booked recurring",
                "=SUMPRODUCT(ConIsLive*ConAnnualValue)", "money",
                span=3, note="Annual value of live contracts")
    row += 1

    # ---------------------------------------------------- the machines --
    row = s.section(row, "Machines, materials and people", LAST_COL)
    s.kpi(row, 0, "Service overdue", "=SUM(EquipServiceDue)", "int",
          note="By hours or by date, whichever came first")
    s.kpi(row, 2, "Service soon", "=SUM(EquipServiceSoon)", "int",
          note="Inside the warning window")
    s.kpi(row, 4, "Out of service",
          '=COUNTIF(EquipStatus,"Out of service")', "int",
          note="Cannot be used at all")
    s.kpi(row, 6, "Materials low", "=SUM(MatIsLow)", "int",
          note="At or below the reorder point")
    s.kpi(row, 8, "Cost to restock", "=SUM(MatOrderValue)", "money",
          note="What the shopping list comes to")
    row = s.kpi(row, 10, "Licences expiring",
                f"={_alert_count('Crew Database', 'Renew -')}+"
                f"{_alert_count('Crew Database', 'Expired -')}",
                "int", span=3, note="Crew tickets about to lapse")
    row += 1

    # ------------------------------------------------- is it working? --
    row = s.section(row, "Is the work paying?", LAST_COL)
    row = s.note(
        row,
        "Revenue is not the test. Profit per crew hour is: it is "
        "what is left after wages, materials, fuel and the "
        "overheads, divided by the hours it took. If it falls while "
        "revenue rises, the extra work is costing you money.",
        LAST_COL, height=34)
    row += 1
    s.kpi(row, 0, "Profit this month",
          '=IFERROR(SUMIFS(ProfitProfit,ProfitMonth,ThisMonthKey),0)',
          "money", note="From the Profit Analysis tab")
    s.kpi(row, 2, "Margin",
          '=IFERROR(SUMIFS(ProfitProfit,ProfitMonth,ThisMonthKey)/'
          'SUMIFS(ProfitRevenue,ProfitMonth,ThisMonthKey),"")',
          "percent0", note="Against your target on Settings")
    s.kpi(row, 4, "Profit per crew hour",
          '=IFERROR(SUMIFS(ProfitProfitHour,ProfitMonth,'
          'ThisMonthKey),"")', "money",
          note="The number that matters most")
    s.kpi(row, 6, "Billable hours",
          '=IFERROR(SUMIFS(ProfitBillablePct,ProfitMonth,'
          'ThisMonthKey),"")', "percent0",
          note="Share of paid time that was sold")
    s.kpi(row, 8, "Quote win rate",
          '=IFERROR(SUM(QuoteIsWon)/(SUM(QuoteIsWon)+'
          'COUNTIF(QuoteStatus,"Declined")),"")', "percent0",
          note="Accepted against answered")
    row = s.kpi(row, 10, "Average visit",
                '=IFERROR(SUMIFS(JobCharge,JobIsDone,1)/'
                'SUM(JobIsDone),"")', "money", span=3,
                note="Across every completed visit")
    row += 1

    # ------------------------------------------------- what needs doing --
    row = s.section(row, "What needs doing", LAST_COL)
    row = s.note(
        row,
        "Every register has a 'What needs doing' column. This is all "
        "sixteen of them added up, by how loudly they are shouting. "
        "Work down from the left.",
        LAST_COL, height=30)
    row += 1
    s.kpi(row, 0, "Urgent", f"={_all_alerts('Urgent -')}", "int",
          note="Something is wrong, not just late")
    s.kpi(row, 2, "Overdue", f"={_all_alerts('Overdue -')}", "int",
          note="Past a date that mattered")
    s.kpi(row, 4, "Chase",
          f"={_all_alerts('Chase -')}+{_all_alerts('Send -')}+"
          f"{_all_alerts('Follow up -')}", "int",
          note="Somebody is waiting on you")
    s.kpi(row, 6, "Schedule",
          f"={_all_alerts('Schedule -')}+"
          f"{_all_alerts('Reschedule -')}", "int",
          note="Work to get in the diary")
    s.kpi(row, 8, "Service & reorder",
          f"={_all_alerts('Service -')}+{_all_alerts('Reorder -')}+"
          f"{_all_alerts('Order -')}+{_all_alerts('Renew -')}", "int",
          note="Machines, materials, contracts")
    row = s.kpi(row, 10, "Tidy up",
                f"={_all_alerts('Add -')}+{_all_alerts('Check -')}+"
                f"{_all_alerts('Action -')}+"
                f"{_all_alerts('Missing -')}", "int", span=3,
                note="Gaps in the record")
    row += 2

    # ------------------------------------------------ today's work list --
    row = s.section(row, "Today's jobs", LAST_COL)
    s.table_head(row, 0,
                 ["Job ID", "Crew", "Start", "Customer", "Address",
                  "Service", "Charge"],
                 widths=[12, 12, 9, 20, 28, 22, 11])
    head = row
    for n in range(1, LIST_ROWS + 1):
        line = head + n
        pick = ('IFERROR(INDEX([[Job & Work Orders.{f}]],'
                'MATCH(ROW()-{h},[[Job & Work Orders.today_rank]],0)),'
                '"")')
        s.formula(line, 0,
                  "=" + pick.format(f="id", h=head + 1),
                  fmts.calc("id"))
        s.formula(line, 1, "=" + pick.format(f="crew", h=head + 1),
                  fmts.calc("text"))
        s.formula(line, 2,
                  '=IFERROR(IF(INDEX([[Job & Work Orders.start_time]],'
                  f'MATCH(ROW()-{head + 1},'
                  '[[Job & Work Orders.today_rank]],0))="","",'
                  'INDEX([[Job & Work Orders.start_time]],'
                  f'MATCH(ROW()-{head + 1},'
                  '[[Job & Work Orders.today_rank]],0))),"")',
                  fmts.calc("time"))
        s.formula(line, 3,
                  "=" + pick.format(f="customer_name", h=head + 1),
                  fmts.calc("text"))
        s.formula(line, 4, "=" + pick.format(f="address", h=head + 1),
                  fmts.calc("text"))
        s.formula(line, 5, "=" + pick.format(f="service", h=head + 1),
                  fmts.calc("text"))
        s.formula(line, 6,
                  '=IFERROR(INDEX([[Job & Work Orders.charge]],'
                  f'MATCH(ROW()-{head + 1},'
                  '[[Job & Work Orders.today_rank]],0))*1,"")',
                  fmts.calc("money"))
    row = head + LIST_ROWS + 2
    row = s.note(
        row,
        "The first eight jobs booked for today, in the order the "
        "Route Planner would print them. Open that tab for the full "
        "day and a sheet the crew can take with them.",
        LAST_COL, height=28)
    row += 1

    # ---------------------------------------------------- chase list --
    row = s.section(row, "Chase these first", LAST_COL)
    s.table_head(row, 0,
                 ["Invoice", "Customer", "Due", "Days late",
                  "Outstanding", "Reminders"],
                 widths=[12, 24, 12, 11, 13, 11])
    head = row
    for n in range(1, LIST_ROWS + 1):
        line = head + n
        s.formula(line, 0,
                  "=" + _by_rank("Invoice & Payments", "late_rank",
                                 "id", f"ROW()-{head + 1}"),
                  fmts.calc("id"))
        s.formula(line, 1,
                  "=" + _by_rank("Invoice & Payments", "late_rank",
                                 "customer_name", f"ROW()-{head + 1}"),
                  fmts.calc("text"))
        s.formula(line, 2,
                  '=IFERROR(IF(INDEX([[Invoice & Payments.due_date]],'
                  f'MATCH(ROW()-{head + 1},'
                  '[[Invoice & Payments.late_rank]],0))="","",'
                  'INDEX([[Invoice & Payments.due_date]],'
                  f'MATCH(ROW()-{head + 1},'
                  '[[Invoice & Payments.late_rank]],0))),"")',
                  fmts.calc("date"))
        s.formula(line, 3,
                  '=IFERROR(INDEX([[Invoice & Payments.days_late]],'
                  f'MATCH(ROW()-{head + 1},'
                  '[[Invoice & Payments.late_rank]],0))*1,"")',
                  fmts.calc("int"))
        s.formula(line, 4,
                  '=IFERROR(INDEX([[Invoice & Payments.outstanding]],'
                  f'MATCH(ROW()-{head + 1},'
                  '[[Invoice & Payments.late_rank]],0))*1,"")',
                  fmts.calc("money"))
        s.formula(line, 5,
                  '=IFERROR(INDEX([[Invoice & Payments.reminders]],'
                  f'MATCH(ROW()-{head + 1},'
                  '[[Invoice & Payments.late_rank]],0))*1,"")',
                  fmts.calc("int"))
    s.cf(f"D{head + 2}:D{head + 1 + LIST_ROWS}",
         {"type": "cell", "criteria": ">=", "value": 30,
          "format": fmts.cf("bad")})
    row = head + LIST_ROWS + 2

    # --------------------------------------------------- best customers --
    row = s.section(row, "Your best customers", LAST_COL)
    s.table_head(row, 0,
                 ["Customer", "Visits", "Lifetime revenue", "Profit",
                  "Margin", "Contract / yr", "Last visit"],
                 widths=[26, 10, 16, 12, 10, 13, 12])
    head = row
    for n in range(1, LIST_ROWS + 1):
        line = head + n
        rank = f"ROW()-{head + 1}"
        s.formula(line, 0,
                  "=" + _by_rank("Customer CRM", "lifetime_rank",
                                 "name", rank), fmts.calc("text"))
        s.formula(line, 1,
                  '=IFERROR(INDEX([[Customer CRM.jobs_done]],'
                  f'MATCH({rank},[[Customer CRM.lifetime_rank]],0))*1,'
                  '"")', fmts.calc("int"))
        s.formula(line, 2,
                  '=IFERROR(INDEX([[Customer CRM.lifetime]],'
                  f'MATCH({rank},[[Customer CRM.lifetime_rank]],0))*1,'
                  '"")', fmts.calc("money"))
        s.formula(line, 3,
                  '=IFERROR(INDEX([[Customer CRM.profit]],'
                  f'MATCH({rank},[[Customer CRM.lifetime_rank]],0))*1,'
                  '"")', fmts.calc("money"))
        s.formula(line, 4,
                  '=IFERROR(INDEX([[Customer CRM.margin_pct]],'
                  f'MATCH({rank},[[Customer CRM.lifetime_rank]],0))*1,'
                  '"")', fmts.calc("percent"))
        s.formula(line, 5,
                  '=IFERROR(INDEX([[Customer CRM.contract_value]],'
                  f'MATCH({rank},[[Customer CRM.lifetime_rank]],0))*1,'
                  '"")', fmts.calc("money"))
        s.formula(line, 6,
                  '=IFERROR(IF(INDEX([[Customer CRM.last_job]],'
                  f'MATCH({rank},[[Customer CRM.lifetime_rank]],0))="",'
                  '"",INDEX([[Customer CRM.last_job]],'
                  f'MATCH({rank},[[Customer CRM.lifetime_rank]],0))),'
                  '"")', fmts.calc("date"))
    row = head + LIST_ROWS + 2

    # ------------------------------------------------------ the honest bit --
    row = s.note(
        row,
        "What this dashboard is not: it does not know about work "
        "nobody has written down. Every figure above is built from "
        "the job, timesheet, expense and invoice rows you have "
        "entered. A week of visits recorded on the back of an "
        "envelope is a week this page cannot see.",
        LAST_COL, height=44)

    s.finish(freeze_row=4, gridlines=False, fit_width=True)
    s.protect()
    return s
````

### `31-landscaping/landscaping_spreadsheet/sheets/equipment.py`
