````python
            Col("contract", "Contract ID", 11, "id",
                validate=pick("ContractIDList",
                              "Pick the agreement this quote became."),
                note="If the quote turned into a recurring agreement, "
                     "put the Contract ID here instead."),
            Col("lost_reason", "If lost, why", 24, "text",
                note="Price, timing, went elsewhere, never replied. Six "
                     "months of this column is worth more than any "
                     "advice about pricing."),
            Col("notes", "Notes", 30, "wrap"),

            Col("is_won", "Won", 6, "int",
                formula=zero("date", f'IF({is_won_quote("{status}{r}")},'
                                     '1,0)'),
                hidden=True),
            Col("is_live", "Live", 6, "int",
                formula=zero("date", f'IF({is_live_quote("{status}{r}")},'
                                     '1,0)'),
                hidden=True),
            Col("is_expired", "Expired", 7, "int",
                formula=zero("date",
                             'IF(AND({is_live}{r}=1,'
                             '{valid_until}{r}<TodayDate),1,0)'),
                hidden=True),
            date_num_col("date", "date_num"),
            month_col("date"),

            Col("alert", "What needs doing", 46, "wrap",
                formula=alert_chain("date", [
                    ('AND({is_won}{r}=1,{job}{r}="",{contract}{r}="")',
                     "Action - accepted but no work order raised yet"),
                    ('{margin_pct}{r}<0',
                     "Loss - this price is below what the job costs"),
                    ('AND({margin_pct}{r}<>"",'
                     '{margin_pct}{r}<MinMargin,{is_live}{r}=1)',
                     "Urgent - margin under your floor, reprice before "
                     "sending"),
                    ('{is_expired}{r}=1',
                     "Expired - past its validity date, call them"),
                    ('AND({is_live}{r}=1,{sent_date}{r}="")',
                     "Send - quote prepared but never sent"),
                    ('AND({is_live}{r}=1,{days_out}{r}>=ChaseQuoteDays)',
                     "Chase - no answer since you sent it"),
                    ('AND({status}{r}="Declined",{lost_reason}{r}="")',
                     "Add - lost, and no reason recorded"),
                    ('{area}{r}=0',
                     "Check - no lawn area on the property record"),
                    ('AND({margin_pct}{r}<>"",'
                     '{margin_pct}{r}<TargetMargin)',
                     "Thin margin - under target, but above your floor"),
                    ('{is_live}{r}=1', "Quoted - waiting on an answer"),
                ]),
                cf=alert_cf()),
        ],
    )
````

### `31-landscaping/landscaping_spreadsheet/sheets/route.py`

<!-- source-file: 31-landscaping/landscaping_spreadsheet/sheets/route.py sha256:25fb5f953b7edc99ceecd94a0d0471509aafcaac955c9b96f7b479fff62a84cd -->
````python
"""`Route Planner` - one crew, one day, one sheet to take with them.

Pick a date and a crew at the top and the day builds itself from the
Job & Work Orders tab: every stop, in the order it is booked, with the
address, the gate code, the dog warning, the service, the time it
should take and what to charge. Print it and hand it over.

What this page is not, and the listing says so too: it is not GPS
navigation and it does not optimise anything. It will not tell you
that visiting Mill Lane before Oak Avenue saves eleven minutes. It
organises the stops you have chosen, in the order you have chosen
them, onto one piece of paper - which is the thing most crews are
actually missing.

Stops are ordered by start time; ties follow job row order and blank
times appear last.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from ..config import CREW_NAMES, Config, Palette
from ..layout import Registry
from ..writer import SheetWriter, date_check

NAME = "Route Planner"
LAST_COL = 10
STOPS = 14


def _stop(field: str, line: int) -> str:
    """Field from the nth job on the chosen crew's chosen day."""
    return (f'IFERROR(INDEX([[Job & Work Orders.{field}]],'
            f'MATCH({line},[[Job & Work Orders.route_match]],0)),"")')


def _stop_num(field: str, line: int) -> str:
    return (f'IFERROR(INDEX([[Job & Work Orders.{field}]],'
            f'MATCH({line},[[Job & Work Orders.route_match]],0))*1,"")')


def build(book, fmts, cfg: Config, reg: Registry) -> SheetWriter:
    s = SheetWriter(book, fmts, cfg, reg, NAME,
                    tab_color=Palette.primary_light)

    s.banner("Route Planner",
             "Pick a day and a crew. The stops, the gate codes and "
             "the times fill themselves in, ready to print.",
             LAST_COL)
    s.set_col(0, 0, 5)
    s.set_col(1, 1, 13)
    s.set_col(2, 2, 24)
    s.set_col(3, 3, 30)
    s.set_col(4, 4, 22)
    s.set_col(5, 5, 9)
    s.set_col(6, 6, 9)
    s.set_col(7, 7, 11)
    s.set_col(8, 8, 16)
    s.set_col(9, LAST_COL, 26)

    row = 4
    row = s.note(
        row,
        "This page organises stops onto a printable sheet. It is not "
        "satellite navigation and it does not work out the shortest "
        "route - you decide the order by setting start times on the "
        "Job & Work Orders tab, and this prints what you decided.",
        LAST_COL, height=34)
    row += 1

    # ------------------------------------------------------- the picker --
    row = s.section(row, "Choose the day", LAST_COL)
    row = s.field(row, "Date", cfg.today, style="date",
                  name="RouteDate", help_col=4,
                  help_text="Type any date. The stops below change "
                            "immediately.",
                  validate=date_check())
    row = s.field(row, "Crew", CREW_NAMES[0] if cfg.include_sample_data else None, name="RouteCrew",
                  help_col=4,
                  validate={"validate": "list",
                            "source": "=CrewNameList",
                            "input_message": "Which crew's day is "
                                             "this?"},
                  help_text="Each crew gets its own sheet. Print one "
                            "per truck.")
    row += 1

    # ---------------------------------------------------- the day's shape --
    row = s.section(row, "The day at a glance", LAST_COL)
    s.kpi(row, 0, "Stops",
          '=COUNTIFS(JobDateNum,RouteDate,JobCrew,RouteCrew,'
          'JobIsOpen,1)', "int", note="Jobs booked, still open")
    s.kpi(row, 2, "Work hours",
          '=SUMIFS(JobHoursEst,JobDateNum,RouteDate,JobCrew,'
          'RouteCrew,JobIsOpen,1)', "number1",
          note="Crew hours on site, estimated")
    s.kpi(row, 4, "Driving",
          '=ROUND(SUMIFS(JobDateNum,JobDateNum,RouteDate,JobCrew,'
          'RouteCrew,JobIsOpen,1)*0+COUNTIFS(JobDateNum,RouteDate,'
          'JobCrew,RouteCrew,JobIsOpen,1)*DriveMinutes/60,1)',
          "number1", note="Rough, at the default hop on Settings")
    s.kpi(row, 6, "Worth",
          '=SUMIFS(JobCharge,JobDateNum,RouteDate,JobCrew,RouteCrew,'
          'JobIsOpen,1)', "money", note="Value of the round")
    row = s.kpi(row, 8, "Per crew hour",
                '=IFERROR(SUMIFS(JobCharge,JobDateNum,RouteDate,'
                'JobCrew,RouteCrew,JobIsOpen,1)/'
                'SUMIFS(JobHoursEst,JobDateNum,RouteDate,JobCrew,'
                'RouteCrew,JobIsOpen,1),"")', "money", span=2,
                note="Against your charge-out rate")
    row += 1

    # ------------------------------------------------------- print head --
    row += 1
    s.merge(row, 0, 5, None, fmts.chrome("print_title"))
    s.formula(row, 0, '=BusinessName&" - crew work order"',
              fmts.chrome("print_title"))
    s.merge(row, 6, LAST_COL, None, fmts.chrome("print_sub"))
    s.formula(row, 6,
              '=TEXT(RouteDate,"dddd d mmmm yyyy")&"   "&RouteCrew',
              fmts.chrome("print_sub"))
    row += 1
    s.merge(row, 0, LAST_COL, None, fmts.chrome("note"))
    s.formula(
        row, 0,
        '="Jobs: "&COUNTIFS(JobDateNum,RouteDate,JobCrew,RouteCrew,'
        'JobIsOpen,1)&"    Estimated hours: "&'
        'TEXT(SUMIFS(JobHoursEst,JobDateNum,RouteDate,JobCrew,'
        'RouteCrew,JobIsOpen,1),"0.0")&'
        '"    Office: "&BusinessPhone',
        fmts.chrome("note"))
    row += 2

    # ------------------------------------------------------- the stops --
    s.table_head(row, 0,
                 ["#", "Start", "Customer", "Address", "Service",
                  "Mins", "Crew", "Charge", "Access / code",
                  "Notes and hazards"],
                 widths=[5, 13, 24, 30, 22, 9, 9, 11, 16, 26])
    head = row
    for n in range(1, STOPS + 1):
        line = head + n
        s.write(line, 0, n, fmts.chrome("line_number"))
        s.formula(line, 1,
                  '=IFERROR(IF(INDEX([[Job & Work Orders.start_time]],'
                  f'MATCH({n},[[Job & Work Orders.route_match]],0))="",'
                  '"",INDEX([[Job & Work Orders.start_time]],'
                  f'MATCH({n},[[Job & Work Orders.route_match]],0))),'
                  '"")', fmts.calc("time"))
        s.formula(line, 2, "=" + _stop("customer_name", n),
                  fmts.calc("text"))
        s.formula(line, 3, "=" + _stop("address", n),
                  fmts.calc("wrap"))
        s.formula(line, 4, "=" + _stop("service", n),
                  fmts.calc("text"))
        s.formula(line, 5,
                  '=IFERROR(ROUND(INDEX('
                  '[[Job & Work Orders.hours_est]],'
                  f'MATCH({n},[[Job & Work Orders.route_match]],0))*60,'
                  '0),"")', fmts.calc("int"))
        s.formula(line, 6, "=" + _stop_num("crew_used", n),
                  fmts.calc("int"))
        s.formula(line, 7, "=" + _stop_num("charge", n),
                  fmts.calc("money"))
        s.formula(line, 8,
                  '=IFERROR(INDEX([[Property Database.gate_code]],'
                  'MATCH(INDEX([[Job & Work Orders.property]],'
                  f'MATCH({n},[[Job & Work Orders.route_match]],0)),'
                  '[[Property Database.id]],0))&"","")',
                  fmts.calc("text"))
        s.formula(line, 9,
                  '=IFERROR(IF(INDEX('
                  '[[Property Database.dog]],'
                  'MATCH(INDEX([[Job & Work Orders.property]],'
                  f'MATCH({n},[[Job & Work Orders.route_match]],0)),'
                  '[[Property Database.id]],0))="Yes","DOG ON SITE. ",'
                  '"")&INDEX([[Property Database.pets_note]],'
                  'MATCH(INDEX([[Job & Work Orders.property]],'
                  f'MATCH({n},[[Job & Work Orders.route_match]],0)),'
                  '[[Property Database.id]],0))&"","")',
                  fmts.calc("wrap"))
        s.row_height(line, 26)
    s.cf(f"J{head + 2}:J{head + 1 + STOPS}",
         {"type": "text", "criteria": "containing", "value": "DOG",
          "format": fmts.cf("bad")})
    row = head + STOPS + 1

    # ------------------------------------------------------- the totals --
    s.write(row, 0, None, fmts.chrome("total_label"))
    s.merge(row, 0, 4, "Day total", fmts.chrome("total_label"))
    s.formula(row, 5,
              '=ROUND(SUMIFS(JobHoursEst,JobDateNum,RouteDate,JobCrew,'
              'RouteCrew,JobIsOpen,1)*60,0)',
              fmts.chrome("total_value"))
    s.write(row, 6, None, fmts.chrome("total_value"))
    s.formula(row, 7,
              '=SUMIFS(JobCharge,JobDateNum,RouteDate,JobCrew,'
              'RouteCrew,JobIsOpen,1)', fmts.chrome("total_value"))
    s.merge(row, 8, LAST_COL, None, fmts.chrome("total_value"))
    row += 2

    # ------------------------------------------- what the crew writes on --
    row = s.section(row, "For the crew to fill in", LAST_COL)
    row = s.note(
        row,
        "Print this page and the crew writes the real times and "
        "anything that went wrong in these boxes. Those numbers go "
        "back into the Timesheets and the job rows that evening, "
        "and that is what makes the profit figures true rather than "
        "hopeful.",
        LAST_COL, height=34)
    row += 1
    s.table_head(row, 0,
                 ["#", "Arrived", "Left", "Actual mins", "Done?",
                  "Problems on site", "Extra work done", "Materials "
                  "used", "Photo taken", "Signature"],
                 widths=[5, 13, 13, 12, 9, 26, 22, 18, 12, 20])
    head = row
    for n in range(1, STOPS + 1):
        line = head + n
        s.write(line, 0, n, fmts.chrome("line_number"))
        for column in range(1, LAST_COL + 1):
            s.write(line, column, None, fmts.chrome("form_line"))
        s.row_height(line, 24)
    row = head + STOPS + 2

    # --------------------------------------------------- the checklist --
    row = s.section(row, "Before you leave each property", LAST_COL)
    row = s.bullets(row, [
        "Gates shut and latched - the single most expensive thing a "
        "crew forgets.",
        "Clippings off the paths, the drive and the road.",
        "Beds and borders edged where the job includes them.",
        "Nothing left behind: strimmer line, fuel cans, hand tools, "
        "the blower.",
        "Any damage photographed and reported the same day, not the "
        "next week.",
        "Customer spoken to if they are in, and told what was done.",
        "Actual time written on this sheet before you drive off.",
    ], LAST_COL)
    row += 1

    row = s.note(
        row,
        "Stops are sorted by start time for the chosen date and crew; "
        "ties follow row order and blank times come last. To change "
        "the order, change the start times on "
        "the Job & Work Orders tab. Stops beyond fourteen in a day "
        "are not printed - if you are regularly over fourteen, split "
        "the round between two crews.",
        LAST_COL, height=34)
    row += 2

    row = _printable_quote(s, fmts, cfg, row)
    row = _printable_invoice(s, fmts, cfg, row)

    s.finish(freeze_row=4, gridlines=False, fit_width=True)
    s.protect()
    return s


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# the two documents a customer actually sees
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def _pull(sheet: str, field: str, key: str, picker: str,
          numeric: bool = False) -> str:
    """One field off the record the picker names."""
    tail = "*1" if numeric else '&""'
    return (f'=IF({picker}="","",IFERROR(INDEX([[{sheet}.{field}]],'
            f'MATCH({picker},[[{sheet}.{key}]],0)){tail},'
            f'{0 if numeric else chr(34) * 2}))')


def _doc_line(s: SheetWriter, fmts, row: int, label: str,
              formula: str, style: str = "text") -> int:
    """`Label | value` inside a printed document."""
    s.merge(row, 1, 2, label, fmts.chrome("form_label"))
    s.merge(row, 3, 6, None, fmts.calc(style))
    s.formula(row, 3, formula, fmts.calc(style))
    return row + 1


def _money_line(s: SheetWriter, fmts, row: int, label: str,
                formula: str, strong: bool = False) -> int:
    """A right-aligned money line on a document."""
    s.merge(row, 4, 6, label,
            fmts.chrome("total_label" if strong else "label_right"))
    s.formula(row, 7, formula,
              fmts.chrome("total_value") if strong
              else fmts.calc("money"))
    return row + 1


def _printable_quote(s: SheetWriter, fmts, cfg: Config, row: int) -> int:
    """A quote on one page, built from the row you name."""
    quote = "Quote Calculator"
    row = s.section(row, "Printable quote - pick one and print it",
                    LAST_COL)
    row = s.field(
        row, "Quote to print",
        "QTE-0001" if cfg.include_sample_data else None,
        name="PrintQuote", help_col=4,
        validate={"validate": "list", "source": "=QuoteIDList",
                  "input_message": "Pick the quote you want on "
                                   "paper."},
        help_text="Every figure below comes from that row of the "
                  "Quote Calculator.")
    row += 1

    s.merge(row, 0, 5, None, fmts.chrome("print_title"))
    s.formula(row, 0, '=BusinessName&" - quote"',
              fmts.chrome("print_title"))
    s.merge(row, 6, LAST_COL, None, fmts.chrome("print_sub"))
    s.formula(row, 6, '="Quote "&PrintQuote&"   "&'
                      'TEXT(TodayDate,"d mmmm yyyy")',
              fmts.chrome("print_sub"))
    row += 1
    s.merge(row, 0, LAST_COL, None, fmts.chrome("note"))
    s.formula(row, 0,
              '=BusinessAddress&", "&BusinessCity&"    "&'
              'BusinessPhone&"    "&BusinessEmail&'
              'IF(BusinessLicence="","","    Licence "&'
              'BusinessLicence)', fmts.chrome("note"))
    row += 2

    row = _doc_line(s, fmts, row, "Quote for",
                    _pull(quote, "customer_name", "id", "PrintQuote"))
    row = _doc_line(s, fmts, row, "Property",
                    _pull(quote, "address", "id", "PrintQuote"))
    row = _doc_line(s, fmts, row, "Work quoted",
                    _pull(quote, "service", "id", "PrintQuote"))
    row = _doc_line(s, fmts, row, "What is included",
                    _pull(quote, "description", "id", "PrintQuote"),
                    style="wrap")
    s.row_height(row - 1, 30)
    row = _doc_line(s, fmts, row, "How often",
                    _pull(quote, "frequency", "id", "PrintQuote"))
    row = _doc_line(
        row=row, s=s, fmts=fmts, label="Time on site",
        formula='=IF(PrintQuote="","",IFERROR(TEXT(INDEX('
                '[[Quote Calculator.site_hours]],MATCH(PrintQuote,'
                '[[Quote Calculator.id]],0)),"0.0")&" hours with "&'
                'INDEX([[Quote Calculator.crew_used]],MATCH('
                'PrintQuote,[[Quote Calculator.id]],0))&" on site",'
                '""))')
    row += 1

    row = _money_line(s, fmts, row, "Price for the visit",
                      _pull(quote, "price_used", "id", "PrintQuote",
                            numeric=True))
    row = _money_line(s, fmts, row, "Discount",
                      _pull(quote, "discount", "id", "PrintQuote",
                            numeric=True))
    s.merge(row, 4, 6, None, fmts.chrome("label_right"))
    s.formula(row, 4, '=IF(TaxOnServices="Yes",TaxName&" at "&'
                      'TEXT(TaxRate,"0.0%"),TaxName)',
              fmts.chrome("label_right"))
    s.formula(row, 7, _pull(quote, "tax", "id", "PrintQuote",
                            numeric=True), fmts.calc("money"))
    row += 1
    row = _money_line(s, fmts, row, "Total",
                      _pull(quote, "total", "id", "PrintQuote",
                            numeric=True), strong=True)
    row = _money_line(
        s, fmts, row, "A year of these visits",
        _pull(quote, "annual_value", "id", "PrintQuote", numeric=True))
    row += 1

    s.merge(row, 0, LAST_COL, None, fmts.chrome("note"))
    s.formula(row, 0,
              '="This quote stands until "&IF(PrintQuote="","",'
              'IFERROR(TEXT(INDEX([[Quote Calculator.valid_until]],'
              'MATCH(PrintQuote,[[Quote Calculator.id]],0)),'
              '"d mmmm yyyy"),""))&". Prices assume reasonable '
              'access and normal growth; anything we find that '
              'changes the work, we will tell you before we do it."',
              fmts.chrome("note"))
    s.row_height(row, 28)
    row += 2
    return row


def _printable_invoice(s: SheetWriter, fmts, cfg: Config,
                       row: int) -> int:
    """An invoice on one page, built from the row you name."""
    inv = "Invoice & Payments"
    row = s.section(row, "Printable invoice - pick one and print it",
                    LAST_COL)
    row = s.note(
        row,
        "This is the document the Invoice & Payments tab refers to. "
        "Pick an invoice, print this block - File, Print, Print "
        "Selection after highlighting it - and record what the "
        "customer pays back on that tab. The workbook cannot send "
        "an email or take a card payment.",
        LAST_COL, height=34)
    row = s.field(
        row, "Invoice to print",
        "INV-00001" if cfg.include_sample_data else None,
        name="PrintInvoice", help_col=4,
        validate={"validate": "list", "source": "=InvoiceIDList",
                  "input_message": "Pick the invoice you want on "
                                   "paper."},
        help_text="Marked on the invoice row as the print line.")
    row += 1

    s.merge(row, 0, 5, None, fmts.chrome("print_title"))
    s.formula(row, 0, '=BusinessName&" - invoice"',
              fmts.chrome("print_title"))
    s.merge(row, 6, LAST_COL, None, fmts.chrome("print_sub"))
    s.formula(row, 6,
              '="Invoice "&IF(PrintInvoice="","",IFERROR(IF(INDEX('
              '[[Invoice & Payments.invoice_number]],MATCH('
              'PrintInvoice,[[Invoice & Payments.id]],0))="",'
              'PrintInvoice,INDEX([[Invoice & Payments.'
              'invoice_number]],MATCH(PrintInvoice,'
              '[[Invoice & Payments.id]],0))),PrintInvoice))',
              fmts.chrome("print_sub"))
    row += 1
    s.merge(row, 0, LAST_COL, None, fmts.chrome("note"))
    s.formula(row, 0,
              '=BusinessAddress&", "&BusinessCity&"    "&'
              'BusinessPhone&"    "&BusinessEmail',
              fmts.chrome("note"))
    row += 2

    row = _doc_line(s, fmts, row, "Bill to",
                    _pull(inv, "customer_name", "id", "PrintInvoice"))
    row = _doc_line(
        s, fmts, row, "Work done",
        _pull(inv, "description", "id", "PrintInvoice"), style="wrap")
    s.row_height(row - 1, 30)
    row = _doc_line(
        s, fmts, row, "Period covered",
        _pull(inv, "period", "id", "PrintInvoice"))
    row = _doc_line(
        s, fmts, row, "Invoice date",
        '=IF(PrintInvoice="","",IFERROR(TEXT(INDEX('
        '[[Invoice & Payments.date]],MATCH(PrintInvoice,'
        '[[Invoice & Payments.id]],0)),"d mmmm yyyy"),""))')
    row = _doc_line(
        s, fmts, row, "Payment due",
        '=IF(PrintInvoice="","",IFERROR(TEXT(INDEX('
        '[[Invoice & Payments.due_date]],MATCH(PrintInvoice,'
        '[[Invoice & Payments.id]],0)),"d mmmm yyyy")&"   ("&'
        'INDEX([[Invoice & Payments.terms]],MATCH(PrintInvoice,'
        '[[Invoice & Payments.id]],0))&")",""))')
    row += 1

    row = _money_line(s, fmts, row, "Net",
                      _pull(inv, "net", "id", "PrintInvoice",
                            numeric=True))
    row = _money_line(s, fmts, row, "Discount",
                      _pull(inv, "discount", "id", "PrintInvoice",
                            numeric=True))
    s.merge(row, 4, 6, None, fmts.chrome("label_right"))
    s.formula(row, 4, '=IF(TaxOnServices="Yes",TaxName&" at "&'
                      'TEXT(TaxRate,"0.0%"),TaxName)',
              fmts.chrome("label_right"))
    s.formula(row, 7, _pull(inv, "tax", "id", "PrintInvoice",
                            numeric=True), fmts.calc("money"))
    row += 1
    row = _money_line(s, fmts, row, "Total",
                      _pull(inv, "total", "id", "PrintInvoice",
                            numeric=True), strong=True)
    row = _money_line(s, fmts, row, "Already paid",
                      _pull(inv, "paid", "id", "PrintInvoice",
                            numeric=True))
    row = _money_line(s, fmts, row, "Now due",
                      _pull(inv, "outstanding", "id", "PrintInvoice",
                            numeric=True), strong=True)
    row += 1

    s.merge(row, 0, LAST_COL, None, fmts.chrome("note"))
    s.formula(row, 0,
              '="Please pay "&CurrencySign&TEXT(IF(PrintInvoice="",'
              '0,IFERROR(INDEX([[Invoice & Payments.outstanding]],'
              'MATCH(PrintInvoice,[[Invoice & Payments.id]],0)),0)),'
              '"#,##0.00")&" to "&BusinessName&" by the due date '
              'above. Questions about this invoice: "&BusinessPhone&'
              '". Thank you for your custom."',
              fmts.chrome("note"))
    s.row_height(row, 28)
    row += 2
    return row
````

### `31-landscaping/landscaping_spreadsheet/sheets/schedule.py`

<!-- source-file: 31-landscaping/landscaping_spreadsheet/sheets/schedule.py sha256:3f44c069d9560b73511f99e0f5f7e3c8d6b49e588f2c83c1baaa1856e3c7576c -->
````python
"""12. Crew Schedule - who is working, and who is already busy.

This is the people side of the week, as opposed to the Route Planner
which is the stops side. One row per person per day: on, off, holiday
or sick, and how many hours they are down for.

The clash column is the point of the tab. It compares the hours
assigned to a person on a day against the jobs actually booked for
their crew that day, so a day that has been promised to two places at
once shows up before the morning it goes wrong.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from ..config import Palette, Config
from ..layout import Col, SheetSpec
from ..sample_data import get as sample
from ..writer import date_check, list_from, time_check
from .common import (alert_cf, alert_chain, amount, date_num_col, id_col,
                     lookup_crew, month_col, pick,
                     scale_cf, week_start_col, weekday_col,
                     yesno, zero)

NAME = "Crew Schedule"


def spec(cfg: Config) -> SheetSpec:
    return SheetSpec(
        name=NAME,
        title="Crew Schedule",
        subtitle="Who is available, who is off, and whether the day "
                 "you have planned actually fits in the hours.",
        tab_color=Palette.primary_mid,
        rows=cfg.row_count("schedule"),
        samples=sample("schedule", cfg),
        freeze_cols=3,
        help_text=(
            "One row per person per working day. Put the date, pick "
            "the person, and say whether they are working. The "
            "'Planned hours' column adds up the jobs already booked "
            "for their crew that day, so you can see at a glance "
            "whether the day is full, empty or impossible."),
        extra_notes=[
            "You do not need a row for every person every day. Most "
            "businesses fill this in a week ahead for the days that "
            "are unusual - holidays, half days, somebody covering "
            "another crew - and leave the ordinary days blank.",
            "Planned hours counts every open job booked to that crew "
            "on that date, using the estimated hours from the "
            "catalogue. Capacity is their available hours. When "
            "planned is bigger than capacity, something will be late.",
        ],
        columns=[
            id_col("date", '"SCH-"', digits=5, header="Line",
                   note="Just a line number, so two identical rows can "
                        "still be told apart."),
            Col("date", "Date", 11, "date",
                validate=date_check(),
                note="Start here."),
            Col("weekday", "Day", 8, "text",
                formula='=IF({date}{r}="","",'
                        'TEXT({date}{r},"ddd"))'),
            Col("employee", "Employee", 11, "id",
                validate=pick("CrewIDList",
                              "Pick the Employee ID from the Crew "
                              "Database."),
                note="Pick from the list, never type it."),
            Col("name", "Name", 20, "text",
                formula=lookup_crew("name")),
            Col("crew", "Crew", 12, "text",
                validate=list_from("CrewNameList"),
                note="Which truck they are on that day. It is not "
                     "always their usual one."),
            Col("working", "Working", 10, "flag",
                validate=yesno("Are they available for work on this "
                               "day?"),
                cf=[{"type": "text", "criteria": "containing",
                     "value": "No", "fmt": "muted"}]),
            Col("reason", "If not, why", 18, "text",
                validate=pick("AbsenceList",
                              "Holiday, sick, training, weather, or a "
                              "day off."),
                note="Six months of this column tells you what your "
                     "real available workforce is, as opposed to the "
                     "one on paper."),
            Col("start_time", "Start", 9, "time",
                validate=time_check()),
            Col("end_time", "End", 9, "time",
                validate=time_check()),
            Col("break_mins", "Break (mins)", 11, "int",
                validate=amount(0, 480, decimal=False)),
            Col("capacity", "Available hrs", 12, "number1",
                formula=zero("date",
                             'IF({working}{r}<>"Yes",0,'
                             'IF(AND({start_time}{r}<>"",'
                             '{end_time}{r}<>""),'
                             'ROUND(({end_time}{r}-{start_time}{r})*24-'
                             '{break_mins}{r}/60,2),WorkingHours))'),
                note="Worked out from the times if you gave them, "
                     "otherwise the standard working day on Settings."),
            Col("planned", "Planned hrs", 11, "number1",
                formula=zero("date",
                             'ROUND(SUMIFS('
                             '[[Job & Work Orders.hours_est]],'
                             '[[Job & Work Orders.date_num]],'
                             '{date}{r},'
                             '[[Job & Work Orders.crew]],{crew}{r},'
                             '[[Job & Work Orders.is_open]],1)/'
                             'MAX(1,CrewSize),2)'),
                cf=scale_cf(),
                note="Every open job booked to this crew on this date, "
                     "shared across the crew. Automatic."),
            Col("jobs_count", "Jobs booked", 11, "int",
                formula=zero("date",
                             'COUNTIFS('
                             '[[Job & Work Orders.date_num]],{date}{r},'
                             '[[Job & Work Orders.crew]],{crew}{r},'
                             '[[Job & Work Orders.is_open]],1)')),
            Col("logged", "Hours logged", 12, "number1",
                formula=zero("date",
                             'SUMIFS('
                             '[[Timesheets & Payroll.hours]],'
                             '[[Timesheets & Payroll.date_num]],'
                             '{date}{r},'
                             '[[Timesheets & Payroll.employee]],'
                             '{employee}{r})'),
                note="What the timesheets say actually happened. The "
                     "other half of the comparison."),
            Col("spare", "Spare hrs", 10, "number1",
                formula='=IF({date}{r}="","",'
                        'ROUND({capacity}{r}-{planned}{r},2))',
                cf=[{"type": "cell", "criteria": "<", "value": -0.01,
                     "fmt": "bold_bad"},
                    {"type": "cell", "criteria": ">=", "value": 2,
                     "fmt": "info"}],
                note="Negative means the day does not fit. Positive by "
                     "a lot means there is room to sell another job."),
            Col("use_pct", "Day used", 9, "percent",
                formula='=IF({date}{r}="","",'
                        'IF({capacity}{r}<=0,"",'
                        'ROUND({planned}{r}/'
                        '{capacity}{r},4)))',
                cf=[{"type": "cell", "criteria": ">", "value": 1,
                     "fmt": "bad"},
                    {"type": "cell", "criteria": ">=", "value": 0.8,
                     "fmt": "good"},
                    {"type": "cell", "criteria": "<", "value": 0.5,
                     "fmt": "warn"}]),
            Col("cost_rate", "Cost / hr", 10, "money",
                formula='=IF({employee}{r}="","",'
                        'IF(IFERROR(INDEX('
                        '[[Crew Database.cost_rate]],'
                        'MATCH({employee}{r},'
                        '[[Crew Database.id]],0))*1,0)>0,'
                        'IFERROR(INDEX([[Crew Database.cost_rate]],'
                        'MATCH({employee}{r},'
                        '[[Crew Database.id]],0))*1,0),LabourRate))',
                hidden=True),
            Col("day_cost", "Cost of day", 11, "money",
                formula=zero("date",
                             'ROUND({capacity}{r}*'
                             'IF({cost_rate}{r}="",LabourRate,'
                             '{cost_rate}{r}),2)'),
                note="What this person's day costs you whether or not "
                     "the work was sold. That is why empty days hurt."),
            Col("notes", "Notes", 28, "wrap"),

            Col("is_future", "Future", 7, "int",
                formula=zero("date",
                             'IF({date}{r}>=TodayDate,1,0)'),
                hidden=True),
            Col("is_over", "Over", 6, "int",
                formula=zero("date",
                             'IF(AND({working}{r}="Yes",'
                             '{spare}{r}<0),1,0)'),
                hidden=True),
            Col("is_idle", "Idle", 6, "int",
                formula=zero("date",
                             'IF(AND({working}{r}="Yes",'
                             '{is_future}{r}=1,{jobs_count}{r}=0),1,0)'),
                hidden=True),
            date_num_col("date", "date_num"),
            weekday_col("date", "dow", header="DOW"),
            week_start_col("date"),
            month_col("date"),

            Col("alert", "What needs doing", 42, "wrap",
                formula=alert_chain("date", [
                    ('AND({working}{r}="Yes",{spare}{r}<-1)',
                     "Clash - more work booked than hours in the day"),
                    ('AND({working}{r}<>"Yes",{jobs_count}{r}>0)',
                     "Urgent - jobs booked for a crew that is off"),
                    ('{is_over}{r}=1',
                     "Over hours - the day is slightly over, check it"),
                    ('{is_idle}{r}=1',
                     "Schedule - available and nothing booked"),
                    ('AND({working}{r}="Yes",{use_pct}{r}<>"",'
                     '{use_pct}{r}<0.5,{is_future}{r}=1)',
                     "Action - less than half the day is sold"),
                    ('AND({working}{r}<>"Yes",{reason}{r}="")',
                     "Add - marked unavailable with no reason"),
                    ('AND({is_future}{r}=0,{logged}{r}=0,'
                     '{working}{r}="Yes")',
                     "Missing - a worked day with no timesheet"),
                ]),
                cf=alert_cf()),
        ],
    )
````

### `31-landscaping/landscaping_spreadsheet/sheets/seasonal.py`

<!-- source-file: 31-landscaping/landscaping_spreadsheet/sheets/seasonal.py sha256:2366bff16035c3e1530f62560af0de5359084e48f9984d782f753e7599436557 -->
````python
"""`Seasonal Planner` - the year, four blocks at a time.

Lawn care is the same twelve months over and over, and almost
everything that goes wrong is something that should have been booked
six weeks earlier. This page is the list: what to sell, what to
service and what to order, season by season, with the numbers from
your own records sitting next to each block so you can see what that
season has actually been worth.

The two checklists at the bottom are the ones crews are most often
missing: a maintenance visit checklist, and a property inspection to
run before quoting a site you have never seen.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from ..config import Config, Palette
from ..layout import Registry
from ..writer import SheetWriter

NAME = "Seasonal Planner"
LAST_COL = 10
TASK_ROWS = 7

#: season -> (months, what to sell, what to prepare)
SEASON_PLAN = [
    ("Spring", "March to May", 3, 5, [
        ("Spring clean-ups", "The biggest selling window of the year. "
                             "Quote these in February, not April."),
        ("First cuts and edging", "Set the round order now and it "
                                  "holds for the whole season."),
        ("Fertiliser and pre-emergent", "Timing beats product. Book "
                                        "it by soil temperature, not "
                                        "by the calendar."),
        ("Mulch and bed refresh", "High margin, and it sells itself "
                                  "once the first warm weekend "
                                  "arrives."),
        ("Aeration and overseeding", "Cool season grass only. Ask "
                                     "before you quote it."),
        ("Irrigation start-up", "Check every head before you turn "
                                "the water on, not after."),
        ("Contract renewals", "Agree this season's price before the "
                              "first cut, never halfway through."),
    ]),
    ("Summer", "June to August", 6, 8, [
        ("Weekly and fortnightly cutting", "The core of the round. "
                                           "Protect it."),
        ("Hedge trimming", "Check for nesting birds first - in many "
                           "places that is the law, not a courtesy."),
        ("Weed control", "Licensed work in most places. Check who on "
                         "the crew can legally do it."),
        ("Irrigation checks", "A dry August is when customers notice "
                              "a head that has not worked since "
                              "May."),
        ("Watering advice", "Free, takes two minutes, and saves the "
                            "lawn you will be blamed for."),
        ("Holiday cover", "Book crew holidays around the round, and "
                          "tell customers before they notice."),
        ("Mid-season equipment service", "The one everybody skips. "
                                         "It is also the one that "
                                         "stops August breakdowns."),
    ]),
    ("Autumn / Fall", "September to November", 9, 11, [
        ("Leaf clearance", "Sell it as a series, not a single "
                           "visit. Three visits beats one argument."),
        ("Autumn feed", "Sets up next spring. Easy to sell to "
                        "anybody who liked their lawn this year."),
        ("Final cuts", "Agree the last cut date in writing so the "
                       "invoice is never a surprise."),
        ("Gutter and drain clearing", "Easy add-on while you are "
                                      "already there with a ladder."),
        ("Irrigation winterising", "Miss it and you will be quoted "
                                   "for the burst pipe."),
        ("Snow contracts", "Sign these in October. Nobody signs a "
                           "snow contract during a blizzard at a "
                           "sensible price."),
        ("Next year's pricing", "Review every contract against this "
                                "year's actual hours."),
    ]),
    ("Winter", "December to February", 12, 2, [
        ("Snow and ice clearing", "If you offer it, agree the "
                                  "trigger depth and the rate "
                                  "before the first fall."),
        ("Pruning and dormant work", "Trees and shrubs are easier to "
                                     "read with no leaves on them."),
        ("Hardscaping and fencing", "Fills the quiet weeks and keeps "
                                    "the crew together."),
        ("Full equipment service", "Every machine, in the workshop, "
                                   "before March. Blades, belts, "
                                   "filters, plugs."),
        ("Book next season", "Ring every customer. The round you "
                             "confirm in January is the round you "
                             "have in April."),
        ("Marketing and quotes", "Spring enquiries start in "
                                 "February. Be ready in January."),
        ("Accounts and insurance", "Renewals, licences, tax. Do it "
                                   "now; you will not have time in "
                                   "May."),
    ]),
]

MAINTENANCE_CHECKLIST = [
    "Walk the property before starting - look for toys, hoses, pet "
    "mess, stones and anything that will become a projectile.",
    "Check the mowing height is right for the season and the grass "
    "type. Scalping in July is how you lose a customer.",
    "Blades sharp and clean. A blunt blade tears the grass and the "
    "lawn goes brown three days later, long after you have left.",
    "Mow in a different direction from last visit where you can - it "
    "stops ruts and keeps the grass standing up.",
    "Edge and strim everything the job includes, every visit. Missed "
    "edges are the most common complaint in this trade.",
    "Blow all hard surfaces clear: paths, drive, patio, and the road "
    "outside.",
    "Clippings dealt with the way the customer agreed - left, bagged "
    "or taken away.",
    "Beds and borders checked for weeds if the job includes them.",
    "Gates closed and latched. Every single time.",
    "Tools counted back onto the trailer before you drive off.",
    "Damage, hazards and anything odd photographed and reported the "
    "same day.",
    "Actual time written down before the next job starts.",
]

INSPECTION_CHECKLIST = [
    "Measure the lawn properly - pace it or use a map tool. Guessing "
    "the area is guessing the price.",
    "Note the slope and the surface. Steep, wet or rough ground can "
    "add half as much again to the time.",
    "Check access: gate width, steps, locked gates, who holds a key, "
    "whether the ride-on can get in at all.",
    "Count the obstacles - trees, beds, play equipment, washing "
    "poles. Every one is a turn and a slow-down.",
    "Look for hazards: ponds, septic lids, irrigation heads, "
    "retaining walls, a bad step, overhead cables.",
    "Ask about dogs, and whether they are out during the day.",
    "Find out where the truck and trailer will park, and whether "
    "there is a time limit.",
    "Check for water and power on site if the work needs them.",
    "Agree what happens to the clippings before you quote, not "
    "after.",
    "Ask what they were unhappy about with the last company. It is "
    "the most useful question you will ask all day.",
    "Photograph the site - before photos are worth money later.",
    "Write the drive time and mileage from your yard onto the "
    "property record.",
]


def build(book, fmts, cfg: Config, reg: Registry) -> SheetWriter:
    s = SheetWriter(book, fmts, cfg, reg, NAME,
                    tab_color=Palette.primary_light)

    s.banner("Seasonal Planner",
             "What to sell, service and order in each season - with "
             "what that season has actually earned you.",
             LAST_COL)
    s.set_col(0, 0, 4)
    s.set_col(1, 1, 30)
    s.set_col(2, 2, 52)
    s.set_col(3, 3, 13)
    s.set_col(4, 4, 13)
    s.set_col(5, LAST_COL, 14)

    row = 4
    row = s.note(
        row,
        "Everything here is a prompt, not a rule. Grass types, "
        "climates and local regulations differ enormously - what "
        "follows is the shape of a temperate season, and you should "
        "edit the tasks to match the ground you actually work on. "
        "The figures on the right are your own, from your own job "
        "records.",
        LAST_COL, height=44)
    row += 1

    # --------------------------------------------------- where we are --
    row = s.section(row, "Right now", LAST_COL)
    s.kpi(row, 0, "Season",
          '=IF(MONTH(TodayDate)<=2,"Winter",'
          'IF(MONTH(TodayDate)<=5,"Spring",'
          'IF(MONTH(TodayDate)<=8,"Summer",'
          'IF(MONTH(TodayDate)<=11,"Autumn / Fall","Winter"))))',
          "text", note="Worked out from today's date")
    s.kpi(row, 2, "In season?",
          '=IF(AND(MONTH(TodayDate)>=SeasonStart,'
          'MONTH(TodayDate)<=SeasonEnd),"Yes - main season",'
          '"No - out of season")', "text",
          note="Against the months on Settings")
    s.kpi(row, 4, "Jobs this month",
          '=COUNTIFS(JobMonth,ThisMonthKey,JobIsDone,1)', "int",
          note="Completed so far")
    s.kpi(row, 6, "Revenue this month",
          '=SUMIFS(JobCharge,JobMonth,ThisMonthKey,JobIsDone,1)',
          "money")
    row = s.kpi(row, 8, "Contracts live",
                "=SUM(ConIsLive)", "int", span=2,
                note="Standing agreements in force")
    row += 1

    # ----------------------------------------------- the four seasons --
    for name, months, first_month, last_month in [
            (p[0], p[1], p[2], p[3]) for p in SEASON_PLAN]:
        plan = dict((p[0], p[4]) for p in SEASON_PLAN)[name]
        row = s.section(row, f"{name}  -  {months}", LAST_COL)

        # the season's own numbers, from the job register
        if first_month <= last_month:
            in_season = (f'(MONTH(JobDateNum)>={first_month})*'
                         f'(MONTH(JobDateNum)<={last_month})')
        else:                      # winter wraps the year end
            in_season = (f'((MONTH(JobDateNum)>={first_month})+'
                         f'(MONTH(JobDateNum)<={last_month}))')
        s.merge(row, 1, 2, "What this season has earned you, all "
                           "years", fmts.chrome("label_bold"))
        s.formula(row, 3,
                  f'=SUMPRODUCT({in_season}*JobIsDone*JobCharge)',
                  fmts.calc("money"))
        s.formula(row, 4,
                  f'=SUMPRODUCT({in_season}*JobIsDone)',
                  fmts.calc("int"))
        s.merge(row, 5, LAST_COL, None, fmts.chrome("note"))
        s.write(row, 5, "Revenue and completed visits in these "
                        "months, from your own records",
                fmts.chrome("note"))
        row += 1

        s.table_head(row, 1, ["Task", "Why it matters", "Start by",
                              "Done?", "Who", "Notes"],
                     widths=[30, 52, 13, 13, 14, 20])
        head = row
        for index, (task, why) in enumerate(plan[:TASK_ROWS]):
            line = head + 1 + index
            s.write(line, 1, task, fmts.chrome("label_bold"))
            s.write(line, 2, why, fmts.chrome("note"))
            s.write(line, 3, None, fmts.input("date"))
            s.write(line, 4, None, fmts.input("flag"))
            s.write(line, 5, None, fmts.input("text"))
            s.merge(line, 6, LAST_COL, None, fmts.input("text"))
            s.ws.data_validation(
                line, 4, line, 4,
                {"validate": "list", "source": ["Yes", "No"]})
            s.row_height(line, 26)
        row = head + len(plan[:TASK_ROWS]) + 2

    # -------------------------------------------- maintenance checklist --
    row = s.section(row, "Lawn maintenance checklist - every visit",
                    LAST_COL)
    row = s.note(
        row,
        "Print this and put it in the truck. Most complaints in this "
        "trade are not about the quality of the cut - they are about "
        "an open gate, a missed edge or clippings on the drive.",
        LAST_COL, height=30)
    row += 1
    s.table_head(row, 1, ["Check", "Done"], widths=[70, 10])
    head = row
    for index, item in enumerate(MAINTENANCE_CHECKLIST):
        line = head + 1 + index
        s.merge(line, 1, 5, item, fmts.chrome("day_item"))
        s.write(line, 6, None, fmts.chrome("form_box"))
        s.row_height(line, 24)
    row = head + len(MAINTENANCE_CHECKLIST) + 2

    # --------------------------------------------- inspection checklist --
    row = s.section(row, "Property inspection checklist - before you "
                         "quote", LAST_COL)
    row = s.note(
        row,
        "Twelve things to establish on a site you have never worked. "
        "Every one of them is a number or a fact that belongs on the "
        "Property Database, and every one of them changes the price.",
        LAST_COL, height=30)
    row += 1
    s.table_head(row, 1, ["Check", "Noted"], widths=[70, 10])
    head = row
    for index, item in enumerate(INSPECTION_CHECKLIST):
        line = head + 1 + index
        s.merge(line, 1, 5, item, fmts.chrome("day_item"))
        s.write(line, 6, None, fmts.chrome("form_box"))
        s.row_height(line, 24)
    row = head + len(INSPECTION_CHECKLIST) + 2

    # ------------------------------------------------ seasonal reminders --
    row = s.section(row, "Reminders that pay for themselves", LAST_COL)
    row = s.bullets(row, [
        "Renew contracts before the season starts, never during it. "
        "A price agreed in February is a conversation; the same "
        "price raised in June is an argument.",
        "Service every machine in the quiet months. A mower that "
        "fails in July costs a week of the best weather of the "
        "year.",
        "Order bulk materials out of season. Mulch and fertiliser "
        "are cheapest when nobody wants them.",
        "Ring dormant customers at the start of spring. The "
        "Customer CRM tab marks them for you after the number of "
        "days you set on Settings.",
        "Check licence and insurance expiry dates in the winter. The "
        "Crew Database warns you sixty days out.",
        "Take before and after photos through the season. In "
        "February they are the only marketing material you will "
        "have.",
    ], LAST_COL)
    row += 1

    row = s.note(
        row,
        "Local regulation beats anything written here. Pesticide "
        "and fertiliser application, hedge cutting during nesting "
        "season, green waste disposal and water use are all "
        "controlled differently from one place to the next, and some "
        "of them carry real penalties. Check what applies where you "
        "work before you sell it.",
        LAST_COL, height=48)

    s.finish(freeze_row=4, gridlines=False, fit_width=True)
    s.protect()
    return s
````

### `31-landscaping/landscaping_spreadsheet/sheets/services.py`

<!-- source-file: 31-landscaping/landscaping_spreadsheet/sheets/services.py sha256:484b1e6995eebaaa35a5c109eb7ece022a01d4ceab21526aea56f25a49aea532 -->
````python
"""6. Service Catalog - your price list, and what each job really costs.

Thirty services come filled in with a rate, a unit and a realistic
time. Change every one of them: these are plausible numbers for a
two-person crew in a mid-cost area, not a recommendation. What the
sheet is really for is the column on the right - the margin each
service earns once the crew, the materials and the overhead are paid.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from ..config import Palette, Config
from ..layout import Col, SheetSpec
from ..sample_data import get as sample
from ..writer import list_from
from .common import (alert_cf, alert_chain, amount, count_by, loss_cf, margin,
                     money_cf, rank_desc, scale_cf, status_cf, sum_by,
                     yesno, zero)

NAME = "Service Catalog"


def spec(cfg: Config) -> SheetSpec:
    return SheetSpec(
        name=NAME,
        title="Service Catalog",
        subtitle="What you sell, what you charge for it, how long it "
                 "takes and what it leaves you with.",
        tab_color=Palette.primary,
        rows=cfg.row_count("services"),
        samples=sample("services", cfg),
        help_text=(
            "The service name is the join key - the quote calculator, "
            "the job register and the contracts all pick from this "
            "list, so renaming a service here renames it everywhere "
            "that has not been written yet, but NOT on rows already "
            "recorded. Add a new line instead of renaming an old one "
            "once you are trading."),
        extra_notes=[
            "'Unit' decides how the quote calculator reads the rate. "
            "Per 1,000 sq ft multiplies by the lawn area; per visit, "
            "per hour and per job do not.",
            "Minutes per unit is your own measured time, and it is the "
            "number that makes a quote honest. If the catalogue says "
            "35 minutes and the timesheets say 50, change the "
            "catalogue.",
            "Margin here is before overhead; the quote calculator adds "
            "overhead per crew hour on top. A service showing 55% here "
            "is nearer 35% once the yard, the insurance and the "
            "paperwork are paid for.",
        ],
        columns=[
            Col("name", "Service", 30, "text",
                note="The name your customers see on the quote. This is "
                     "the join key - keep it short and keep it stable."),
            Col("category", "Category", 18, "text",
                validate=list_from("ServiceCategoryList")),
            Col("description", "What it includes", 40, "wrap",
                note="Worth writing properly: this is what stops the "
                     "'I thought that included the hedges' conversation."),
            Col("unit", "Priced per", 17, "text",
                validate=list_from("PricingUnitList"),
                note="How the rate is read. 'Per 1,000 sq ft' multiplies "
                     "by the lawn area; 'Per visit' does not."),
            Col("rate", "Your rate", 11, "money",
                validate=amount(0, 100000),
                note="What you charge for one unit. Every price in the "
                     "workbook starts here."),
            Col("minutes", "Minutes per unit", 13, "int",
                validate=amount(0, 10000),
                note="Your own measured time for one unit of this "
                     "service, for one person."),
            Col("crew_size", "Crew needed", 11, "int",
                validate=amount(1, 20),
                note="How many people it takes. Two people for 30 "
                     "minutes is one crew hour, not half of one."),
            Col("materials_cost", "Materials per unit", 14, "money",
                validate=amount(0, 100000),
                note="Fertiliser, mulch, seed, bags. Leave at 0 for "
                     "pure labour services like mowing."),
            Col("equipment", "Main equipment", 20, "text",
                validate=list_from("EquipmentCategoryList"),
                note="What has to be on the trailer. Useful when a "
                     "machine goes in for repair and you need to know "
                     "which jobs are affected."),
            Col("min_charge", "Minimum charge", 12, "money",
                validate=amount(0, 100000),
                note="The least you will turn out for. Blank uses the "
                     "minimum visit charge on Settings."),
            Col("season", "Main season", 15, "text",
                validate=list_from("SeasonList"),
                note="When this sells. Drives the seasonal planner."),
            Col("frequency", "Usual frequency", 16, "text",
                validate=list_from("FrequencyList"),
                note="How often a customer typically buys it."),
            Col("taxable", "Taxable", 9, "flag",
                validate=yesno("Is this service subject to sales tax or "
                               "VAT where you trade?"),
                note="Rules differ by state and country, and mowing is "
                     "not always treated the same as landscaping. Ask "
                     "your accountant, then set this."),
            Col("skill", "Skill needed", 16, "text",
                validate=list_from("CrewRoleList"),
                note="Who on the crew can actually do it. Pesticide work "
                     "needs the licence."),
            Col("licence_needed", "Licence needed", 12, "flag",
                validate=yesno("Does this service require a pesticide or "
                               "trade licence?"),
                note="If Yes, only licensed crew should be assigned."),
            Col("status", "Status", 12, "text",
                validate=list_from("ServiceStatusList"),
                cf=status_cf()),
            Col("notes", "Notes", 30, "wrap"),

            # ---- the economics ---------------------------------------
            Col("hours_per_unit", "Crew hours", 10, "number1",
                formula=zero("name",
                             'ROUND({minutes}{r}*MAX(1,{crew_size}{r})'
                             '/60,2)'),
                note="Minutes times the number of people, in hours. This "
                     "is what the labour actually costs you."),
            Col("labour_cost", "Labour cost", 11, "money",
                formula=zero("name",
                             'ROUND({hours_per_unit}{r}*LabourRate,2)'),
                note="At the crew rate on Settings. Set a real loaded "
                     "rate there - wage plus tax plus insurance."),
            Col("overhead_cost", "Overhead", 10, "money",
                formula=zero("name",
                             'ROUND({hours_per_unit}{r}*OverheadRate,2)'),
                note="The yard, the insurance and the office, charged "
                     "by the crew hour."),
            Col("total_cost", "Cost per unit", 12, "money",
                formula=zero("name",
                             'ROUND({labour_cost}{r}+{materials_cost}{r}'
                             '+{overhead_cost}{r},2)'),
                note="Everything except the drive, which depends on the "
                     "property."),
            Col("profit_unit", "Profit per unit", 13, "money",
                formula=zero("name",
                             'ROUND({rate}{r}-{total_cost}{r},2)'),
                cf=loss_cf()),
            Col("margin_pct", "Margin", 9, "percent",
                formula='=IF({name}{r}="","",'
                        f'{margin("{profit_unit}{r}", "{rate}{r}")})',
                cf=[{"type": "cell", "criteria": ">=",
                     "value": "=TargetMargin", "fmt": "good"},
                    {"type": "cell", "criteria": "<",
                     "value": "=MinMargin", "fmt": "bad"},
                    {"type": "cell", "criteria": "<",
                     "value": "=TargetMargin", "fmt": "warn"}],
                note="Green at or above your target, red below your "
                     "floor. Both are set on Settings."),
            Col("per_hour", "Earns per hour", 12, "money",
                formula='=IF({name}{r}="","",'
                        'IF({hours_per_unit}{r}<=0,"",'
                        'ROUND({rate}{r}/'
                        '{hours_per_unit}{r},2)))',
                cf=[{"type": "cell", "criteria": ">=",
                     "value": "=ChargeRate", "fmt": "good"},
                    {"type": "cell", "criteria": "<",
                     "value": "=ChargeRate", "fmt": "warn"}],
                note="The one number to compare services on. A service "
                     "earning below your charge-out rate is underpriced, "
                     "however good the margin looks."),
            Col("suggested", "Suggested rate", 13, "money",
                formula=zero("name",
                             'ROUND({total_cost}{r}/'
                             'MAX(0.05,1-TargetMargin),2)'),
                note="What this rate would have to be to hit your target "
                     "margin. A suggestion, not a price - the market has "
                     "a vote."),
            Col("gap", "Rate gap", 10, "money",
                formula=zero("name",
                             'ROUND({rate}{r}-{suggested}{r},2)'),
                cf=loss_cf(),
                note="Negative means you are charging less than your own "
                     "target says you should."),

            # ---- how it is selling -----------------------------------
            Col("times_sold", "Visits done", 11, "int",
                formula=zero("name", count_by("Job & Work Orders",
                                              "service", '{name}{r}',
                                              "is_done", "1")),
                cf=scale_cf()),
            Col("revenue", "Revenue", 12, "money",
                formula=zero("name", sum_by("Job & Work Orders", "charge",
                                            "service", '{name}{r}',
                                            "is_done", "1")),
                cf=money_cf()),
            Col("quoted", "Times quoted", 11, "int",
                formula=zero("name", count_by("Quote Calculator",
                                              "service", '{name}{r}'))),
            Col("won", "Quotes won", 10, "int",
                formula=zero("name", count_by("Quote Calculator",
                                              "service", '{name}{r}',
                                              "is_won", "1"))),
            Col("win_rate", "Win rate", 9, "percent",
                formula='=IF({name}{r}="","",'
                        'IF({quoted}{r}<=0,"",'
                        'ROUND({won}{r}/{quoted}{r},4)))',
                cf=scale_cf(),
                note="Winning everything usually means the price is too "
                     "low, not that the selling is good."),
            Col("avg_actual", "Actual hours avg", 13, "number1",
                formula='=IF({name}{r}="","",'
                        'IFERROR(AVERAGEIFS('
                        '[[Job & Work Orders.hours_actual]],'
                        '[[Job & Work Orders.service]],{name}{r},'
                        '[[Job & Work Orders.is_done]],1,'
                        '[[Job & Work Orders.hours_actual]],">0"),""))',
                note="What this service really takes, from the "
                     "timesheets. The reality check on the estimate."),
            Col("contracts", "On contract", 10, "int",
                formula=zero("name", count_by("Recurring Contracts",
                                              "service", '{name}{r}',
                                              "is_live", "1"))),
            Col("is_active", "Active", 7, "int",
                formula=zero("name", 'IF({status}{r}="Active",1,0)'),
                hidden=True),
            rank_desc("revenue", guard='{name}{r}=""'),

            Col("alert", "What needs doing", 44, "wrap",
                formula=alert_chain("name", [
                    ('{rate}{r}=0', "Add - no rate set for this service"),
                    ('{minutes}{r}=0',
                     "Add - no time set, so it cannot be scheduled "
                     "honestly"),
                    ('{profit_unit}{r}<0',
                     "Loss - this service costs more than it charges"),
                    ('AND({margin_pct}{r}<>"",{margin_pct}{r}<MinMargin)',
                     "Urgent - margin is below your floor, reprice it"),
                    ('AND({avg_actual}{r}<>"",{hours_per_unit}{r}>0,'
                     '{avg_actual}{r}>{hours_per_unit}{r}*1.25)',
                     "Check - it really takes longer than the catalogue "
                     "says"),
                    ('AND({quoted}{r}>=5,{win_rate}{r}<>"",'
                     '{win_rate}{r}<0.2)',
                     "Check - rarely accepted, the price may be too "
                     "high"),
                    ('AND({quoted}{r}>=5,{win_rate}{r}<>"",'
                     '{win_rate}{r}>0.9)',
                     "Action - you win nearly every one, test a higher "
                     "price"),
                    ('AND({margin_pct}{r}<>"",'
                     '{margin_pct}{r}<TargetMargin)',
                     "Thin margin - under your target, review the rate"),
                    ('AND({is_active}{r}=1,{times_sold}{r}=0,'
                     '{quoted}{r}=0)',
                     "Action - never sold or quoted, is it worth "
                     "offering?"),
                    ('{description}{r}=""',
                     "Add - no description, so the quote is vague"),
                ]),
                cf=alert_cf()),
        ],
    )
````

### `31-landscaping/landscaping_spreadsheet/sheets/settings.py`

<!-- source-file: 31-landscaping/landscaping_spreadsheet/sheets/settings.py sha256:5f2611e3c6dcde5a2d78622a9028b9a4752db6ec3390f2bfe09befbc1b779925 -->
````python
"""`Settings & Lists` - every number and every list the workbook runs on.

Nothing here is hard coded to one country, one currency or one way of
running a lawn care round. Your crew rate, your charge-out rate, your
minimum visit, your travel rate, your margin floor, your service
intervals and all fifty-odd drop-downs are set here, once, and every
other tab follows.

Three groups deserve a second look before you start.

The crew cost rate should be the loaded cost - wages plus payroll tax
plus insurance - not what lands in somebody's bank account. Put the
take-home figure in and every job in this workbook will look more
profitable than it is.

The overhead per crew hour is the one most people leave at zero. The
yard, the truck insurance, the phone, the accountant and the evenings
doing paperwork are all real, and a three-hour visit carries three
hours of them whether or not anybody works it out.

The ID prefixes decide what your Customer IDs, Property IDs, Job IDs
and Invoice IDs look like. Change them before you have typed two
hundred customers, not after.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import datetime as _dt
from typing import List, Tuple

from ..config import (ABSENCE_REASONS, ACCESS_TYPES, CONTRACT_STATUSES,
                      CREW_NAMES, CREW_ROLES, CREW_STATUSES, CURRENCIES,
                      CUSTOMER_STATUSES, CUSTOMER_TYPES, DEFAULT_VEHICLES,
                      DISCLAIMER, EMPLOYMENT_TYPES, EQUIPMENT_CATEGORIES,
                      EQUIPMENT_CONDITIONS, EQUIPMENT_STATUSES,
                      EXPENSE_CATEGORIES, FEEDBACK_CAUSES,
                      FEEDBACK_SOURCES, FEEDBACK_STATUSES, FEEDBACK_TYPES,
                      FREQUENCIES, HONESTY_NOTE, ID_PREFIX_FIELDS,
                      INVOICE_STATUSES, JOB_STATUSES, LEAD_SOURCES,
                      MAINTENANCE_TYPES, MATERIAL_CATEGORIES,
                      MATERIAL_STATUSES, MATERIAL_UNITS, MONTH_NAMES,
                      PAYMENT_METHODS, PAYMENT_TERMS, PAYROLL_NOTE,
                      PHOTO_NOTE, PRICING_UNITS, PRIORITIES, PRIVACY_NOTE,
                      PROPERTY_STATUSES, PROPERTY_TYPES, QUOTE_STATUSES,
                      ROUTE_NOTE, SEASONS, SERVICE_CATEGORIES,
                      SERVICE_STATUSES, STOCK_MOVES, TASK_TYPES,
                      TAX_CATEGORIES, TERRAIN_TYPES, VEHICLE_COST_TYPES,
                      WEATHER_CONDITIONS, WEATHER_NOTE, WEEKDAYS, YES_NO,
                      Config, Palette)
from ..layout import Registry, col_letter, dynamic_name, quote_sheet
from ..writer import SheetWriter, list_from, number_check, yes_no

NAME = "Settings & Lists"
LAST_COL = 11

#: name -> values. Every drop-down in the workbook comes from this table.
LISTS: List[Tuple[str, List[str]]] = [
    ("YesNoList", list(YES_NO)),
    ("CustomerTypeList", list(CUSTOMER_TYPES)),
    ("CustomerStatusList", list(CUSTOMER_STATUSES)),
    ("LeadSourceList", list(LEAD_SOURCES)),
    ("PropertyTypeList", list(PROPERTY_TYPES)),
    ("PropertyStatusList", list(PROPERTY_STATUSES)),
    ("TerrainList", list(TERRAIN_TYPES)),
    ("AccessList", list(ACCESS_TYPES)),
    ("ServiceCategoryList", list(SERVICE_CATEGORIES)),
    ("ServiceStatusList", list(SERVICE_STATUSES)),
    ("PricingUnitList", list(PRICING_UNITS)),
    ("QuoteStatusList", list(QUOTE_STATUSES)),
    ("JobStatusList", list(JOB_STATUSES)),
    ("PriorityList", list(PRIORITIES)),
    ("WeatherList", list(WEATHER_CONDITIONS)),
    ("ContractStatusList", list(CONTRACT_STATUSES)),
    ("CrewNameList", list(CREW_NAMES)),
    ("CrewRoleList", list(CREW_ROLES)),
    ("CrewStatusList", list(CREW_STATUSES)),
    ("EmploymentTypeList", list(EMPLOYMENT_TYPES)),
    ("AbsenceList", list(ABSENCE_REASONS)),
    ("TaskTypeList", list(TASK_TYPES)),
    ("EquipmentCategoryList", list(EQUIPMENT_CATEGORIES)),
    ("EquipmentStatusList", list(EQUIPMENT_STATUSES)),
    ("EquipmentConditionList", list(EQUIPMENT_CONDITIONS)),
    ("MaintenanceTypeList", list(MAINTENANCE_TYPES)),
    ("VehicleList", list(DEFAULT_VEHICLES)),
    ("VehicleCostList", list(VEHICLE_COST_TYPES)),
    ("MaterialCategoryList", list(MATERIAL_CATEGORIES)),
    ("MaterialUnitList", list(MATERIAL_UNITS)),
    ("MaterialStatusList", list(MATERIAL_STATUSES)),
    ("StockMoveList", list(STOCK_MOVES)),
    ("InvoiceStatusList", list(INVOICE_STATUSES)),
    ("PaymentMethodList", list(PAYMENT_METHODS)),
    ("ExpenseCategoryList", list(EXPENSE_CATEGORIES)),
    ("TaxCategoryList", list(TAX_CATEGORIES)),
    ("FeedbackSourceList", list(FEEDBACK_SOURCES)),
    ("FeedbackTypeList", list(FEEDBACK_TYPES)),
    ("FeedbackStatusList", list(FEEDBACK_STATUSES)),
    ("FeedbackCauseList", list(FEEDBACK_CAUSES)),
    ("SeasonList", list(SEASONS)),
    ("WeekdayList", list(WEEKDAYS)),
    ("MonthNameList", list(MONTH_NAMES)),
    ("CurrencyList", list(CURRENCIES)),
]


def _month_keys(today: _dt.date, back: int = 18,
                ahead: int = 18) -> List[str]:
    """`yyyy-mm` keys around today - what every monthly total groups on."""
    start = today.year * 12 + today.month - 1 - back
    return [f"{(start + n) // 12:04d}-{(start + n) % 12 + 1:02d}"
            for n in range(back + ahead + 1)]


def build(book, fmts, cfg: Config, reg: Registry) -> SheetWriter:
    s = SheetWriter(book, fmts, cfg, reg, NAME, tab_color=Palette.ink)
    sheet_ref = quote_sheet(NAME)

    s.banner("Settings & Lists",
             "Your business, your rates, your rules, your lists. Set "
             "these once and all twenty-three tabs follow.",
             LAST_COL)
    s.set_col(0, 0, 3)
    s.set_col(1, 2, 30)
    s.set_col(3, 3, 18)
    s.set_col(4, LAST_COL, 17)

    row = 4
    row = s.note(
        row,
        "White cells are yours to change; everything else is locked "
        "and calculated. Nothing here assumes a country, a currency "
        "or a size of business - put your own rates, your own "
        "margins and your own service intervals in, and the rest of "
        "the workbook follows.",
        LAST_COL, height=34)
    row += 1

    # ------------------------------------------------------ business --
    row = s.section(row, "Your business", LAST_COL)
    row = s.field(row, "Business name", cfg.business.name,
                  name="BusinessName", value_end=5, help_col=7,
                  help_text="Printed at the top of every quote, "
                            "invoice and crew work order.")
    row = s.field(row, "Owner", cfg.business.owner, name="OwnerName",
                  value_end=5, help_col=7)
    row = s.field(row, "Email", cfg.business.email,
                  name="BusinessEmail", value_end=5, help_col=7)
    row = s.field(row, "Phone", cfg.business.phone,
                  name="BusinessPhone", value_end=5, help_col=7)
    row = s.field(row, "Website", cfg.business.website, value_end=5,
                  help_col=7)
    row = s.field(row, "Yard / depot address", cfg.business.address_1,
                  name="BusinessAddress", value_end=5, help_col=7,
                  help_text="Where the trucks start from. Travel "
                            "distances on the Property Database are "
                            "measured from here.")
    row = s.field(row, "Address line 2", cfg.business.address_2,
                  value_end=5, help_col=7)
    row = s.field(row, "City", cfg.business.city, name="BusinessCity",
                  value_end=5, help_col=7)
    row = s.field(row, "Region / state", cfg.business.region,
                  value_end=5, help_col=7)
    row = s.field(row, "Zip / postcode", cfg.business.postcode)
    row = s.field(row, "Country", cfg.business.country, value_end=5,
                  help_col=7)
    row = s.field(row, "Tax / VAT number", cfg.business.tax_id,
                  value_end=5, help_col=7)
    row = s.field(row, "Licence number", cfg.business.licence,
                  name="BusinessLicence", value_end=5, help_col=7,
                  help_text="Pesticide applicator or contractor "
                            "licence, if your state or country "
                            "requires one on the paperwork.")
    row = s.field(row, "Insurance policy", cfg.business.insurance,
                  value_end=5, help_col=7,
                  help_text="Liability policy number. Commercial "
                            "customers ask for it.")
    row = s.field(row, "Currency symbol", cfg.currency,
                  name="CurrencySign",
                  help_text="Shown on screen. The cell formats "
                            "follow the symbol you build the file "
                            "with.")
    row = s.field(row, "Currency code", cfg.currency_code,
                  validate=list_from("CurrencyList"))
    row = s.field(row, "Today", None, style="date", name="TodayDate",
                  mode="calc", formula="=TODAY()",
                  help_text="Live. Everything that says 'overdue', "
                            "'due soon' or 'this week' reads this "
                            "one cell.")
    row = s.field(row, "Reporting year", cfg.report_year, style="int",
                  name="ReportYear", validate=number_check(2000, 2100),
                  help_text="The year the Profit Analysis, Monthly "
                            "and Annual reports cover.")
    row = s.field(row, "Year starts", None, style="date",
                  name="YearStart", mode="calc",
                  formula="=DATE(ReportYear,1,1)")
    row = s.field(row, "Year ends", None, style="date",
                  name="YearEnd", mode="calc",
                  formula="=DATE(ReportYear,12,31)")
    row = s.field(row, "This month", None, style="text",
                  name="ThisMonthKey", mode="calc",
                  formula='=TEXT(TODAY(),"yyyy-mm")',
                  help_text="The month key every monthly total "
                            "groups on.")
    row += 1

    # ------------------------------------------------- labour rates --
    row = s.section(row, "What labour costs you", LAST_COL)
    row = s.note(
        row,
        "The crew cost rate is the most important number in this "
        "workbook and the one most often set too low. It is the "
        "loaded cost of an hour of somebody's time - wages, payroll "
        "tax, insurance, holiday, the share of the truck they ride "
        "in - not the figure on their payslip. A $20 wage usually "
        "costs a business between $26 and $30.",
        LAST_COL, height=46)
    row += 1
    row = s.field(row, "Crew cost per hour", cfg.labour_rate,
                  style="money", name="LabourRate",
                  validate=number_check(0, 1000),
                  help_text="Used wherever a person on the Crew "
                            "Database has no rate of their own.")
    row = s.field(row, "Charge-out rate per hour", cfg.charge_rate,
                  style="money", name="ChargeRate",
                  validate=number_check(0, 1000),
                  help_text="What an hour of crew time is worth to "
                            "a customer. Every 'earns per hour' "
                            "column in the workbook is measured "
                            "against this.")
    row = s.field(row, "Overhead per crew hour", cfg.overhead_per_hour,
                  style="money", name="OverheadRate",
                  validate=number_check(0, 1000),
                  help_text="The yard, the insurance, the phone and "
                            "the paperwork, spread over the hours "
                            "you actually work. Take your yearly "
                            "overheads and divide by your billable "
                            "hours - most small operations land "
                            "between $8 and $15.")
    row = s.field(row, "Standard working day", cfg.working_hours_day,
                  style="number1", name="WorkingHours",
                  validate=number_check(1, 24),
                  help_text="Hours in a normal day, used by the crew "
                            "schedule when no times are given.")
    row = s.field(row, "Overtime after", cfg.overtime_after_hours,
                  style="number1", name="OvertimeAfter",
                  validate=number_check(0, 168),
                  help_text="Hours per person per week before "
                            "overtime starts. An indicator for your "
                            "own planning - your payroll provider is "
                            "the authority on overtime law.")
    row = s.field(row, "Overtime multiplier", cfg.overtime_multiplier,
                  style="number1", name="OvertimeRate",
                  validate=number_check(1, 5))
    row = s.field(row, "Default crew size", cfg.crew_size, style="int",
                  name="CrewSize", validate=number_check(1, 20),
                  help_text="How many people go out on a normal "
                            "job.")
    row += 1

    # --------------------------------------------------- the pricing --
    row = s.section(row, "How you price work", LAST_COL)
    row = s.note(
        row,
        "The quote calculator works out what a job costs you, then "
        "adds the target margin. The minimum margin is the line "
        "below which the workbook starts calling a price a problem - "
        "on a quote, on a service, on a customer and on a contract.",
        LAST_COL, height=38)
    row += 1
    row = s.field(row, "Target profit margin", cfg.target_margin,
                  style="percent", name="TargetMargin",
                  validate=number_check(0, 0.95),
                  help_text="Margin, not markup. 45% margin is the "
                            "same as a 1.82 multiplier on cost.")
    row = s.field(row, "Minimum acceptable margin", cfg.minimum_margin,
                  style="percent", name="MinMargin",
                  validate=number_check(0, 0.95),
                  help_text="Anything below this is flagged in red "
                            "wherever it appears.")
    row = s.field(row, "Minimum visit charge", cfg.minimum_visit,
                  style="money", name="MinimumVisit",
                  validate=number_check(0, 10000),
                  help_text="The least you will turn out for. The "
                            "quote calculator uses it as a floor.")
    row = s.field(row, "Materials markup", cfg.material_markup,
                  style="number1", name="MaterialMarkup",
                  validate=number_check(1, 10),
                  help_text="Multiplier on what materials cost you. "
                            "1.35 means a $100 pallet of mulch is "
                            "charged at $135 - collecting, carrying "
                            "and spreading are real work.")
    row = s.field(row, "Travel rate per mile", cfg.travel_rate_mile,
                  style="money", name="TravelRate",
                  validate=number_check(0, 100),
                  help_text="Fuel, tyres and the share of the truck. "
                            "Charged on the round trip, both ways.")
    row = s.field(row, "Default drive time", cfg.drive_time_minutes,
                  style="int", name="DriveMinutes",
                  validate=number_check(0, 600),
                  help_text="Minutes each way, used when a property "
                            "has no drive time of its own.")
    row = s.field(row, "Mowing minutes per 1,000 sq ft",
                  cfg.mow_minutes_per_1000, style="number1",
````
