````python
                  name="MowMinutesPer1000",
                  validate=number_check(0, 600),
                  help_text="Your own measured pace with your own "
                            "machine, for one person. Used to "
                            "estimate mow time on the Property "
                            "Database.")
    row = s.field(row, "Quote valid for", cfg.quote_valid_days,
                  style="int", name="QuoteValidDays",
                  validate=number_check(1, 365),
                  help_text="Days before a quote expires on its own.")
    row += 1

    # ------------------------------------------------------- the tax --
    row = s.section(row, "Tax", LAST_COL)
    row = s.note(
        row,
        "Whether lawn care is taxable where you trade is a question "
        "for your accountant, and the answer differs by state and by "
        "country - mowing and landscaping are often treated "
        "differently from each other. Switch tax on only when you "
        "know which applies to you, and set the rate you are "
        "actually registered for.",
        LAST_COL, height=46)
    row += 1
    row = s.field(row, "Charge tax on services?",
                  "Yes" if cfg.tax_on_services else "No",
                  name="TaxOnServices", validate=yes_no(),
                  help_text="No means no tax is added anywhere in "
                            "the workbook.")
    row = s.field(row, "Tax rate", cfg.tax_rate, style="percent",
                  name="TaxRate", validate=number_check(0, 1))
    row = s.field(row, "What you call it", cfg.tax_name,
                  name="TaxName", value_end=5,
                  help_text="Sales tax, VAT, GST - whatever appears "
                            "on your paperwork.")
    row += 1

    # -------------------------------------------------- when to warn --
    row = s.section(row, "When the workbook should warn you", LAST_COL)
    row = s.note(
        row,
        "Every 'due', 'overdue' and 'chase' message in the workbook "
        "is measured against one of these. Make them match how you "
        "actually work - a round that runs a fortnight ahead needs a "
        "different upcoming window from one booked the night before.",
        LAST_COL, height=38)
    row += 1
    row = s.field(row, "Upcoming window", cfg.upcoming_days,
                  style="int", name="UpcomingDays",
                  validate=number_check(1, 90),
                  help_text="Days ahead counted as 'coming up' on "
                            "the dashboard.")
    row = s.field(row, "Invoice overdue after", cfg.overdue_days,
                  style="int", name="OverdueDays",
                  validate=number_check(0, 90),
                  help_text="Days past the due date before an "
                            "invoice is called overdue.")
    row = s.field(row, "Chase a quote after", cfg.chase_quote_days,
                  style="int", name="ChaseQuoteDays",
                  validate=number_check(1, 180),
                  help_text="Days with no answer before the quote "
                            "appears on the chase list.")
    row = s.field(row, "Contract renewal warning",
                  cfg.renewal_warning_days, style="int",
                  name="RenewalWarnDays", validate=number_check(1, 365),
                  help_text="Days before a review or end date that "
                            "the reminder starts.")
    row = s.field(row, "Customer dormant after", cfg.dormant_days,
                  style="int", name="DormantDays",
                  validate=number_check(7, 999),
                  help_text="Days since the last completed visit "
                            "before a customer is called dormant.")
    row = s.field(row, "Chase a review after", cfg.feedback_chase_days,
                  style="int", name="FeedbackChaseDays",
                  validate=number_check(1, 180))
    row += 1

    # --------------------------------------------------- the machines --
    row = s.section(row, "Equipment servicing", LAST_COL)
    row = s.note(
        row,
        "Mowers measure their lives in engine hours and everything "
        "else measures it in months, so the workbook tracks both and "
        "warns on whichever comes first. These are the defaults; any "
        "machine can carry its own interval on the Equipment "
        "Inventory tab.",
        LAST_COL, height=38)
    row += 1
    row = s.field(row, "Service every (hours)", cfg.service_hours,
                  style="int", name="ServiceHours",
                  validate=number_check(1, 10000),
                  help_text="Engine hours between services. Check "
                            "the manual - 50 to 100 hours is "
                            "typical for commercial mowers.")
    row = s.field(row, "Service every (months)", cfg.service_months,
                  style="int", name="ServiceMonths",
                  validate=number_check(1, 120))
    row = s.field(row, "Warn this many hours before",
                  cfg.service_warning_hours, style="int",
                  name="ServiceWarnHours", validate=number_check(0, 500))
    row = s.field(row, "Warn this many days before",
                  cfg.service_warning_days, style="int",
                  name="ServiceWarnDays", validate=number_check(0, 365))
    row += 1

    # ---------------------------------------------------- the season --
    row = s.section(row, "Your season and your targets", LAST_COL)
    row = s.field(row, "Season starts (month)", cfg.season_start_month,
                  style="int", name="SeasonStart",
                  validate=number_check(1, 12),
                  help_text="The first month of your main cutting "
                            "season. 3 is March.")
    row = s.field(row, "Season ends (month)", cfg.season_end_month,
                  style="int", name="SeasonEnd",
                  validate=number_check(1, 12),
                  help_text="The last month. 11 is November.")
    row = s.field(row, "Revenue target for the year",
                  cfg.target_revenue_year, style="money",
                  name="RevenueTarget",
                  validate=number_check(0, 100000000),
                  help_text="What you want the year to bring in. The "
                            "monthly target is a twelfth of this "
                            "unless you set your own.")
    row = s.field(row, "Jobs per week target", cfg.target_jobs_week,
                  style="int", name="JobsTarget",
                  validate=number_check(0, 1000))
    row = s.field(row, "Fuel price per gallon", cfg.fuel_price,
                  style="money", name="FuelPrice",
                  validate=number_check(0, 100),
                  help_text="For estimating. Actual spend comes off "
                            "the Vehicle & Fuel Tracker.")
    row += 2

    # ------------------------------------------- payment terms table --
    row = s.section(row, "Payment terms", LAST_COL)
    row = s.note(
        row,
        "What each term means in days. Every invoice works out its "
        "own due date from this table, so if your 'Net 30' really "
        "means thirty days from the end of the month, change the "
        "number here. 'Monthly in advance' is negative because the "
        "money is due before the work.",
        LAST_COL, height=38)
    row += 1
    terms_head = row
    s.table_head(terms_head, 1, ["Term", "Days"], widths=[26, 14])
    first_term = terms_head + 1
    for index, (label, days) in enumerate(PAYMENT_TERMS):
        line = first_term + index
        s.write(line, 1, label, fmts.input("text"))
        s.write(line, 2, days, fmts.input("int"))
    last_term = first_term + len(PAYMENT_TERMS) - 1
    book.define_name(
        "PaymentTermsList",
        f"={sheet_ref}!$B${first_term + 1}:$B${last_term + 1}")
    book.define_name(
        "TermDays",
        f"={sheet_ref}!$C${first_term + 1}:$C${last_term + 1}")
    row = last_term + 2

    # ----------------------------------------------- frequency table --
    row = s.section(row, "How often work repeats", LAST_COL)
    row = s.note(
        row,
        "This table turns 'Fortnightly' into a number of visits and "
        "a number of days. The contracts tab uses the days to work "
        "out when the next visit is due, and the annual value of "
        "every agreement is the price per visit times the visits a "
        "year. 'One-off' is zero on both counts.",
        LAST_COL, height=38)
    row += 1
    freq_head = row
    s.table_head(freq_head, 1,
                 ["How often", "Visits a year", "Days between"],
                 widths=[24, 16, 16])
    first_freq = freq_head + 1
    for index, (label, per_year, gap) in enumerate(FREQUENCIES):
        line = first_freq + index
        s.write(line, 1, label, fmts.input("text"))
        s.write(line, 2, per_year, fmts.input("int"))
        s.write(line, 3, gap, fmts.input("int"))
    last_freq = first_freq + len(FREQUENCIES) - 1
    book.define_name(
        "FrequencyList",
        f"={sheet_ref}!$B${first_freq + 1}:$B${last_freq + 1}")
    book.define_name(
        "VisitsPerYear",
        f"={sheet_ref}!$C${first_freq + 1}:$C${last_freq + 1}")
    book.define_name(
        "DaysBetween",
        f"={sheet_ref}!$D${first_freq + 1}:$D${last_freq + 1}")
    row = last_freq + 2

    # -------------------------------------------------------- prefixes --
    row = s.section(row, "ID prefixes", LAST_COL)
    row = s.note(
        row,
        "The letters in front of every automatic ID. These are the "
        "keys the workbook joins on - Customer IDs, Property IDs, "
        "Job IDs and Invoice IDs above all. Change the prefixes here "
        "if you want to, but do it before you have typed two hundred "
        "customers, not after: existing rows keep the ID they were "
        "given.",
        LAST_COL, height=44)
    row += 1
    half = (len(ID_PREFIX_FIELDS) + 1) // 2
    top = row
    for index, (label, default, name, _digits, hint) in enumerate(
            ID_PREFIX_FIELDS):
        column = 0 if index < half else 4
        line = top + (index if index < half else index - half)
        s.write(line, column + 1, label, fmts.chrome("label_bold"))
        s.write(line, column + 2, default, fmts.input("text"))
        s.write(line, column + 3, hint, fmts.chrome("note"))
        book.define_name(
            name, f"={sheet_ref}!${col_letter(column + 2)}${line + 1}")
    row = top + half + 1

    # ----------------------------------------------------------- lists --
    row = s.section(row, "Drop-down lists", LAST_COL)
    row = s.note(
        row,
        "Add new entries directly under the last one in a column - "
        "every list has room to grow and blank rows are ignored. Do "
        "not delete a whole column: a drop-down pointing at a "
        "missing list stops working. The crew names and vehicle "
        "names are yours to rename - 'Crew A' and 'Truck 1' are "
        "only a starting point.",
        LAST_COL, height=44)
    row += 1

    per_row = 4
    spare = 6
    top = row
    column = 0
    tallest = 0
    for index, (name, values) in enumerate(LISTS):
        if index and index % per_row == 0:
            top += tallest + 2
            column = 0
            tallest = 0
        s.write(top, column, name.replace("List", ""),
                fmts.chrome("header"))
        s.set_col(column, column, 28)
        for offset, value in enumerate(values):
            s.write(top + 1 + offset, column, value, fmts.input("text"))
        for offset in range(len(values), len(values) + spare):
            s.write(top + 1 + offset, column, None, fmts.input("text"))
        first = top + 2
        last = top + 1 + len(values) + spare
        book.define_name(
            name,
            f"={sheet_ref}!${col_letter(column)}${first}:"
            f"${col_letter(column)}${last}")
        tallest = max(tallest, len(values) + spare)
        column += 3
    row = top + tallest + 3

    # ------------------------------------------------------ month keys --
    row = s.section(row, "Month keys", LAST_COL)
    row = s.note(
        row,
        "The months the reports pick from, in plain yyyy-mm text so "
        "that every monthly total in the workbook groups on exactly "
        "the same thing.",
        LAST_COL, height=28)
    row += 1
    keys = _month_keys(cfg.today)
    s.write(row, 0, "Month", fmts.chrome("header"))
    s.set_col(0, 0, 14)
    # Keep the dropdown relevant when the reporting year changes.
    for offset, _key in enumerate(keys):
        s.formula(row + 1 + offset, 0,
                  f'=TEXT(DATE(ReportYear-1,{offset + 1},1),"yyyy-mm")',
                  fmts.calc("text"))
    book.define_name(
        "MonthKeyList",
        f"={sheet_ref}!$A${row + 2}:$A${row + 1 + len(keys)}")
    book.define_name(
        "MonthKeys",
        dynamic_name(NAME, "A", row + 2, row + 1 + len(keys)))
    row = row + len(keys) + 2

    row = s.note(row, ROUTE_NOTE, LAST_COL, height=62)
    row += 1
    row = s.note(row, PAYROLL_NOTE, LAST_COL, height=56)
    row += 1
    row = s.note(row, WEATHER_NOTE, LAST_COL, height=48)
    row += 1
    row = s.note(row, PHOTO_NOTE, LAST_COL, height=48)
    row += 1
    row = s.note(row, HONESTY_NOTE, LAST_COL, height=68)
    row += 1
    row = s.note(row, PRIVACY_NOTE, LAST_COL, height=56)
    row += 1
    row = s.note(row, DISCLAIMER, LAST_COL, height=76)

    s.finish(freeze_row=4, gridlines=False, fit_width=True)
    s.protect()
    return s
````

### `31-landscaping/landscaping_spreadsheet/sheets/timesheets.py`

<!-- source-file: 31-landscaping/landscaping_spreadsheet/sheets/timesheets.py sha256:4191e6aa7eaad94792f37a939bc3f10abb01f2439e9d77378e3e3666628976c6 -->
````python
"""13. Timesheets & Payroll - the hours, and what they really cost.

Every line is one person, one day, and usually one job. Hours booked
against a Job ID flow straight into that job's actual cost, which is
what makes the estimated-versus-actual comparison possible at all.

Hours that are not against a job - driving, yard time, mending a
mower, quoting - still cost money and are still recorded here. They
are what the billable percentage measures, and that percentage
explains more bad months than any other number in the workbook.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from ..config import Palette, Config
from ..layout import Col, SheetSpec
from ..sample_data import get as sample
from ..writer import date_check, time_check
from .common import (alert_cf, alert_chain, amount, date_num_col, id_col,
                     lookup_crew, money_cf,
                     month_col, pick, scale_cf, week_start_col,
                     weekday_col, yesno, zero)

NAME = "Timesheets & Payroll"


def spec(cfg: Config) -> SheetSpec:
    return SheetSpec(
        name=NAME,
        title="Timesheets & Payroll",
        subtitle="Hours by person, by day and by job - costed at each "
                 "person's own rate, and fed back into job profit.",
        tab_color=Palette.primary_mid,
        rows=cfg.row_count("timesheets"),
        samples=sample("timesheets", cfg),
        freeze_cols=3,
        help_text=(
            "One line per person per job per day. Put the Job ID on "
            "it and the hours cost that job automatically. Leave the "
            "Job ID blank for travel, yard work or anything else that "
            "is not chargeable - it still costs you, and it still "
            "belongs here."),
        extra_notes=[
            "Hours can be entered either as a start and finish time "
            "or as a plain number of hours. If both are present the "
            "times win, because they are the harder thing to "
            "misremember.",
            "Overtime is worked out per person per week against the "
            "threshold on Settings, and costed at the multiplier. It "
            "is an indicator for your own planning, not a payroll "
            "calculation - overtime law varies and your payroll "
            "provider is the authority on it. Enter rows in chronological "
            "order for each employee and week: overtime is allocated in "
            "row order, so late backdated entries can change job costs.",
            "This tab does not file taxes, produce payslips or "
            "report to any payroll service. It records what was "
            "worked so that your job costs are honest.",
        ],
        columns=[
            id_col("date", '"TS-"', digits=5, header="Line"),
            Col("date", "Date", 11, "date",
                validate=date_check(),
                note="Start here."),
            Col("employee", "Employee", 11, "id",
                validate=pick("CrewIDList",
                              "Pick the Employee ID from the Crew "
                              "Database."),
                note="Pick from the list. Their own cost rate is used."),
            Col("name", "Name", 20, "text",
                formula=lookup_crew("name")),
            Col("job", "Job ID", 11, "id",
                validate=pick("JobIDList",
                              "Pick the job these hours were worked "
                              "on."),
                note="The job these hours belong to. Leave blank for "
                     "non-chargeable time - that is not a mistake, it "
                     "is the point of the billable column."),
            Col("job_address", "Where", 26, "text",
                formula='=IF({job}{r}="","",'
                        'IFERROR(INDEX('
                        '[[Job & Work Orders.address]],'
                        'MATCH({job}{r},'
                        '[[Job & Work Orders.id]],0))&"",'
                        '"Check - Job ID not found"))',
                cf=[{"type": "text", "criteria": "containing",
                     "value": "Check -", "fmt": "bad"}]),
            Col("task", "What they did", 22, "text",
                validate=pick("TaskTypeList",
                              "Mowing, driving, maintenance, quoting, "
                              "yard work."),
                note="Non-job time is worth classifying. It is where "
                     "the day goes."),
            Col("start_time", "Start", 9, "time",
                validate=time_check()),
            Col("end_time", "End", 9, "time",
                validate=time_check()),
            Col("break_mins", "Break", 8, "int",
                validate=amount(0, 480, decimal=False)),
            Col("hours_typed", "Hours", 9, "number1",
                validate=amount(0, 24,
                                "Hours worked, if you are not using "
                                "start and finish times."),
                note="Use this or the times, whichever suits. Not "
                     "both."),
            Col("hours", "Hours used", 11, "number1",
                formula=zero("date",
                             'IF(AND({start_time}{r}<>"",'
                             '{end_time}{r}<>""),'
                             'ROUND(MAX(0,MOD({end_time}{r}-'
                             '{start_time}{r},1)*24-'
                             '{break_mins}{r}/60),2),'
                             '{hours_typed}{r})'),
                cf=scale_cf(),
                note="From the times if they are there, otherwise the "
                     "typed figure."),
            Col("week_hours", "Week to date", 12, "number1",
                formula=zero("date",
                             'SUMIFS({hours_first}:{hours_last},'
                             '{employee_first}:{employee_last},'
                             '{employee}{r},'
                             '{week_start_first}:{week_start_last},'
                             '{week_start}{r})'),
                hidden=True,
                note="This person's hours in the same week, used to "
                     "work out where overtime starts."),
            Col("week_before", "Week before line", 12, "number1",
                formula=zero("date",
                             'SUMIFS({hours_first}:{hours}{r},'
                             '{employee_first}:{employee}{r},'
                             '{employee}{r},'
                             '{week_start_first}:{week_start}{r},'
                             '{week_start}{r})-{hours}{r}'),
                hidden=True),
            Col("overtime_hours", "Overtime", 10, "number1",
                formula=zero("date",
                             'ROUND(MAX(0,{week_before}{r}+'
                             '{hours}{r}-OvertimeAfter)-'
                             'MAX(0,{week_before}{r}-OvertimeAfter),2)'),
                cf=[{"type": "cell", "criteria": ">", "value": 0,
                     "fmt": "warn"}],
                note="The part of this line that falls past the weekly "
                     "threshold on Settings."),
            Col("normal_hours", "Normal hours", 11, "number1",
                formula=zero("date",
                             'ROUND({hours}{r}-'
                             '{overtime_hours}{r},2)'),
                hidden=True),
            Col("rate", "Cost / hr", 10, "money",
                formula=zero("date",
                             'IF(IFERROR(INDEX('
                             '[[Crew Database.cost_rate]],'
                             'MATCH({employee}{r},'
                             '[[Crew Database.id]],0))*1,0)>0,'
                             'IFERROR(INDEX('
                             '[[Crew Database.cost_rate]],'
                             'MATCH({employee}{r},'
                             '[[Crew Database.id]],0))*1,0),'
                             'LabourRate)'),
                note="Their loaded rate from the Crew Database, or the "
                     "default on Settings if it is blank."),
            Col("ot_multiplier", "Overtime x", 10, "number1",
                formula=zero("date",
                             'IF(IFERROR(INDEX('
                             '[[Crew Database.overtime_rate]],'
                             'MATCH({employee}{r},'
                             '[[Crew Database.id]],0))*1,0)>0,'
                             'IFERROR(INDEX('
                             '[[Crew Database.overtime_rate]],'
                             'MATCH({employee}{r},'
                             '[[Crew Database.id]],0))*1,0),'
                             'OvertimeRate)'),
                hidden=True),
            Col("cost", "Cost", 11, "money",
                formula=zero("date",
                             'ROUND({normal_hours}{r}*{rate}{r}+'
                             '{overtime_hours}{r}*{rate}{r}*'
                             '{ot_multiplier}{r},2)'),
                cf=money_cf(),
                note="What this line costs the business. Lines with a "
                     "Job ID land on that job's actual cost."),
            Col("pay", "Gross pay", 11, "money",
                formula=zero("date",
                             'ROUND(({normal_hours}{r}+'
                             '{overtime_hours}{r}*'
                             '{ot_multiplier}{r})*'
                             'IFERROR(INDEX('
                             '[[Crew Database.pay_rate]],'
                             'MATCH({employee}{r},'
                             '[[Crew Database.id]],0))*1,0),2)'),
                note="At their wage rate, for your own reference. Not "
                     "a payslip, and no tax is calculated."),
            Col("mileage", "Miles driven", 11, "number1",
                validate=amount(0, 2000),
                note="Personal vehicle miles to reimburse, if that is "
                     "how you work."),
            Col("approved", "Approved", 10, "flag",
                validate=yesno("Have you checked and approved this "
                               "line?"),
                cf=[{"type": "text", "criteria": "containing",
                     "value": "No", "fmt": "warn"}]),
            Col("notes", "Notes", 26, "wrap"),

            # ---- the bits other tabs read ----------------------------
            Col("is_billable", "Billable", 8, "int",
                formula=zero("date",
                             'IF(AND({job}{r}<>"",{hours}{r}>0),1,0)'),
                hidden=True),
            Col("job_value", "Job value share", 12, "money",
                formula=zero("date",
                             'IF({is_billable}{r}=0,0,'
                             'ROUND(IFERROR(INDEX('
                             '[[Job & Work Orders.charge]],'
                             'MATCH({job}{r},'
                             '[[Job & Work Orders.id]],0))*1,0)*'
                             '{hours}{r}/MAX({hours}{r},SUMIFS('
                             '{hours_first}:{hours_last},'
                             '{job_first}:{job_last},{job}{r})),2))'),
                hidden=True,
                note="This line's share of what the job was worth, "
                     "split by hours. Used for the crew scorecard."),
            date_num_col("date", "date_num"),
            weekday_col("date", "dow", header="DOW"),
            week_start_col("date"),
            month_col("date"),

            Col("alert", "What needs doing", 42, "wrap",
                formula=alert_chain("date", [
                    ('{job_address}{r}="Check - Job ID not found"',
                     "Check - the Job ID on this line does not exist"),
                    ('{hours}{r}=0',
                     "Add - no hours on this line"),
                    ('{hours}{r}>14',
                     "Check - more than fourteen hours in one day"),
                    ('{rate}{r}=0',
                     "Add - no cost rate for this person"),
                    ('{overtime_hours}{r}>0',
                     "Over hours - part of this line is overtime"),
                    ('AND({job}{r}="",{task}{r}="")',
                     "Add - non-job time with no explanation"),
                    ('{approved}{r}<>"Yes"',
                     "Check - not approved yet"),
                ]),
                cf=alert_cf()),
        ],
    )
````

### `31-landscaping/landscaping_spreadsheet/sheets/vehicles.py`

<!-- source-file: 31-landscaping/landscaping_spreadsheet/sheets/vehicles.py sha256:7c555405da2617dcfc889f60f34aa9680b5509688305e4a58bdac8ca6d06032c -->
````python
"""15. Vehicle & Fuel Tracker - every fill-up and every repair.

One row per fill-up or per vehicle cost. Record the odometer each
time and the workbook works out the miles between fills and the
economy you are actually getting, which is the earliest warning you
will get that something is wrong with a truck.

Fuel entered here also lands on the expense reports, so it is
counted once and only once.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from ..config import Palette, Config
from ..layout import Col, SheetSpec
from ..sample_data import get as sample
from ..writer import date_check
from .common import (alert_cf, alert_chain, amount, date_num_col, id_col,
                     money_cf, month_col, pick, scale_cf, yesno, zero)

NAME = "Vehicle & Fuel Tracker"


def spec(cfg: Config) -> SheetSpec:
    return SheetSpec(
        name=NAME,
        title="Vehicle & Fuel Tracker",
        subtitle="Fill-ups, repairs, tax and insurance - by vehicle, "
                 "with the economy you are really getting.",
        tab_color=Palette.accent,
        rows=cfg.row_count("vehicles"),
        samples=sample("vehicles", cfg),
        freeze_cols=3,
        help_text=(
            "One line per fill-up or per vehicle bill. Put the "
            "odometer reading on every fuel line and the miles per "
            "gallon work themselves out from one fill to the next. "
            "Set up your vehicles in the list on the Settings tab "
            "first."),
        extra_notes=[
            "Economy is calculated between consecutive fill-ups for "
            "the same vehicle, so the first fill for each one shows "
            "nothing. That is correct, not a fault.",
            "A truck whose economy drops by a fifth is telling you "
            "something - tyres, a dragging brake, a trailer loaded "
            "wrong, or a driver with a heavy foot.",
            "Costs recorded here flow into the expense reports "
            "automatically. Do not enter the same fuel receipt on "
            "the Expense Tracker as well or it will be counted "
            "twice.",
        ],
        columns=[
            id_col("date", '"VEH-"', digits=5, header="Line"),
            Col("date", "Date", 11, "date",
                validate=date_check(),
                note="Start here."),
            Col("vehicle", "Vehicle", 16, "text",
                validate=pick("VehicleList",
                              "Pick the vehicle. The list is on the "
                              "Settings tab."),
                note="Pick from the list so one truck's history stays "
                     "in one place."),
            Col("type", "Cost type", 16, "text",
                validate=pick("VehicleCostList",
                              "Fuel, service, repair, tyres, "
                              "insurance, tax, cleaning."),
                note="Fuel lines get the economy treatment; the rest "
                     "are just costs."),
            Col("odometer", "Odometer", 11, "int",
                validate=amount(0, 2000000, decimal=False),
                note="The reading at the pump. Put it on every fuel "
                     "line and the economy columns do the rest."),
            Col("gallons", "Gallons / litres", 13, "number1",
                validate=amount(0, 1000,
                                "How much fuel went in. Use whichever "
                                "unit you buy in, consistently."),
                note="Whatever unit you buy in - just be consistent, "
                     "because the economy figure follows it."),
            Col("amount", "Cost", 11, "money",
                validate=amount(0, 1000000),
                cf=money_cf(),
                note="What you paid."),
            Col("unit_price", "Price per unit", 12, "money",
                formula='=IF({date}{r}="","",'
                        'IF({gallons}{r}<=0,"",'
                        'ROUND({amount}{r}/'
                        '{gallons}{r},3)))',
                note="Worth watching over a season. Fuel is usually "
                     "the third biggest cost in this trade."),
            Col("full_tank", "Filled up", 10, "flag",
                validate=yesno("Was the tank filled right up? Economy "
                               "is only meaningful between full "
                               "tanks."),
                note="Part fills make the economy figure meaningless, "
                     "so they are skipped."),
            Col("driver", "Driver", 16, "text",
                note="Who was driving. Useful when one truck's economy "
                     "is oddly worse than the other's."),
            Col("supplier", "Where", 18, "text"),
            Col("reference", "Receipt / invoice", 16, "text"),
            Col("job", "Job ID", 11, "id",
                validate=pick("JobIDList",
                              "Pick the job, if this cost belongs to "
                              "one."),
                note="Only if this cost belongs to one job - a special "
                     "trip to the tip, for instance. Usually blank."),
            Col("notes", "Notes", 26, "wrap"),

            # ---- the economy -----------------------------------------
            Col("is_fuel", "Fuel", 6, "int",
                formula=zero("date",
                             'IF(AND({type}{r}="Fuel",'
                             '{gallons}{r}>0,{odometer}{r}>0),1,0)'),
                hidden=True),
            Col("prev_odo", "Previous odo", 11, "int",
                formula=zero("date",
                             'IF({is_fuel}{r}=0,0,'
                             'SUMPRODUCT(MAX('
                             '({vehicle_first}:{vehicle_last}='
                             '{vehicle}{r})*'
                             '({is_fuel_first}:{is_fuel_last}=1)*'
                             '({odometer_first}:{odometer_last}<'
                             '{odometer}{r})*'
                             '{odometer_first}:{odometer_last})))'),
                hidden=True,
                note="The highest lower odometer reading for the same "
                     "vehicle - where this tank started. Works out by "
                     "reading, not by row, so entering a receipt late "
                     "does not break it."),
            Col("miles", "Miles on tank", 12, "int",
                formula='=IF({date}{r}="","",'
                        'IF({prev_odo}{r}<=0,"",'
                        '{odometer}{r}-{prev_odo}{r}))',
                note="Blank on the first fill for each vehicle, which "
                     "is as it should be."),
            Col("economy", "Miles per unit", 13, "number1",
                formula='=IF({date}{r}="","",'
                        'IF({is_fuel}{r}=0,"",'
                        'IF({full_tank}{r}<>"Yes","",'
                        'IF({prev_odo}{r}<=0,"",'
                        'ROUND(({odometer}{r}-'
                        '{prev_odo}{r})/{gallons}{r},2)))))',
                cf=scale_cf(),
                note="Only on full tanks with a previous reading to "
                     "measure from."),
            Col("cost_per_mile", "Cost per mile", 12, "money",
                formula='=IF({date}{r}="","",'
                        'IF({miles}{r}="","",'
                        'IF({miles}{r}<=0,"",'
                        'ROUND({amount}{r}/'
                        '{miles}{r},3))))'),
            Col("vehicle_avg", "Vehicle average", 13, "number1",
                formula='=IF({date}{r}="","",'
                        'IF({is_fuel}{r}=0,"",'
                        'IFERROR(AVERAGEIFS('
                        '{economy_first}:{economy_last},'
                        '{vehicle_first}:{vehicle_last},'
                        '{vehicle}{r},'
                        '{economy_first}:{economy_last},">0"),"")))',
                hidden=True),
            Col("economy_gap", "vs average", 10, "percent",
                formula='=IF({date}{r}="","",'
                        'IF({economy}{r}="","",'
                        'IF({vehicle_avg}{r}="","",'
                        'IF({vehicle_avg}{r}<=0,"",'
                        'ROUND({economy}{r}/'
                        '{vehicle_avg}{r}-1,4)))))',
                cf=[{"type": "cell", "criteria": "<", "value": -0.15,
                     "fmt": "bad"},
                    {"type": "cell", "criteria": ">", "value": 0.1,
                     "fmt": "good"}],
                note="How this tank compares with that vehicle's "
                     "normal. A run of red is worth investigating."),
            date_num_col("date", "date_num"),
            month_col("date"),

            Col("alert", "What needs doing", 42, "wrap",
                formula=alert_chain("date", [
                    ('AND({type}{r}="Fuel",{odometer}{r}=0)',
                     "Add - no odometer reading, so economy cannot be "
                     "worked out"),
                    ('{amount}{r}=0', "Add - no cost on this line"),
                    ('AND({economy_gap}{r}<>"",'
                     '{economy_gap}{r}<-0.15)',
                     "Check - economy well below this vehicle's "
                     "average"),
                    ('AND({type}{r}="Fuel",{gallons}{r}=0)',
                     "Add - no quantity, so price per unit is blank"),
                    ('AND({prev_odo}{r}>0,{odometer}{r}<'
                     '{prev_odo}{r})',
                     "Check - odometer lower than a previous reading"),
                    ('{reference}{r}=""',
                     "Add - no receipt reference recorded"),
                ]),
                cf=alert_cf()),
        ],
    )
````

### `31-landscaping/landscaping_spreadsheet/writer.py`

<!-- source-file: 31-landscaping/landscaping_spreadsheet/writer.py sha256:4090d8f1bd2e724f1485708cd25ff9231dcd80ea2b39dffeb9011b5964c94a06 -->
````python
"""
Sheet writing helpers shared by every tab of the workbook.

:class:`SheetWriter` wraps an XlsxWriter worksheet and adds the house style:
title band, navigation strip, section headers, KPI tiles, label/value settings
rows and - most importantly - :meth:`SheetWriter.grid`, which turns a
:class:`~daycare_business_spreadsheet.layout.SheetSpec` into a finished register
with headers, drop downs, conditional formats, sample rows, frozen panes and
locked formula cells.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import datetime as _dt
from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional, Sequence, Tuple

from .config import Config, Palette
from .formats import CALC, FormatBook, INPUT, PLAIN
from .layout import (NAV_ROW, SUBTITLE_ROW, TITLE_ROW, Registry,
                     SheetSpec, col_letter, quote_sheet)

P = Palette

#: Sheets linked from the navigation strip at the top of every tab.
NAV_LINKS: List[Tuple[str, str]] = [
    ("Dashboard", "Dashboard"),
    ("Start", "Getting Started"),
    ("Customers", "Customer CRM"),
    ("Properties", "Property Database"),
    ("Services", "Service Catalog"),
    ("Quotes", "Quote Calculator"),
    ("Jobs", "Job & Work Orders"),
    ("Route", "Route Planner"),
    ("Contracts", "Recurring Contracts"),
    ("Crew", "Crew Database"),
    ("Timesheets", "Timesheets & Payroll"),
    ("Equipment", "Equipment Inventory"),
    ("Invoices", "Invoice & Payments"),
    ("Profit", "Profit Analysis"),
    ("Settings", "Settings & Lists"),
]

#: Worksheet protection: formulas are locked, everything else stays usable.
PROTECT_OPTIONS: Dict[str, bool] = {
    "objects": False,
    "scenarios": False,
    "format_cells": True,
    "format_columns": True,
    "format_rows": True,
    "insert_columns": False,
    "insert_rows": False,
    "insert_hyperlinks": True,
    "delete_columns": False,
    "delete_rows": False,
    "select_locked_cells": True,
    "sort": False,          # stops rows being re-sorted out of sync with IDs
    "autofilter": True,     # filtering stays available
    "pivot_tables": False,
    "select_unlocked_cells": True,
}


class SheetWriter:
    """Convenience wrapper around a worksheet."""

    def __init__(self, book, fmts: FormatBook, cfg: Config, reg: Registry,
                 name: str, tab_color: Optional[str] = None,
                 landscape: bool = True) -> None:
        self.book = book
        self.f = fmts
        self.cfg = cfg
        self.reg = reg
        self.name = name
        self.ws = book.add_worksheet(name)
        self._protected = False
        if tab_color:
            self.ws.set_tab_color(tab_color)
        if landscape:
            self.ws.set_landscape()
        self.ws.set_paper(9)  # A4
        self.ws.set_margins(0.4, 0.4, 0.6, 0.5)
        self.ws.set_header(
            f"&L&\"Calibri,Bold\"&12{''}"
            f"&C&\"Calibri,Bold\"&11{name}"
            f"&R&\"Calibri,Italic\"&9{cfg.product_name}")
        self.ws.set_footer(
            f"&L&\"Calibri,Italic\"&8{cfg.author} - v{cfg.version}"
            "&C&\"Calibri,Italic\"&8Page &P of &N"
            "&R&\"Calibri,Italic\"&8&D")

    # ------------------------------------------------------------- plumbing
    def write(self, row: int, col: int, value: Any, fmt=None):
        """Type aware write (0 based row/col, like XlsxWriter)."""
        if value is None:
            if fmt is not None:
                self.ws.write_blank(row, col, None, fmt)
            return
        if isinstance(value, str) and value.startswith("="):
            self.ws.write_formula(row, col, value.strip(), fmt)
        elif isinstance(value, (_dt.datetime, _dt.date, _dt.time)):
            self.ws.write_datetime(row, col, value, fmt)
        elif isinstance(value, bool):
            self.ws.write_string(row, col, "Yes" if value else "No", fmt)
        elif isinstance(value, (int, float)):
            self.ws.write_number(row, col, value, fmt)
        else:
            self.ws.write_string(row, col, str(value), fmt)

    def cf(self, cell_range: str, rule: Dict[str, Any]):
        """Apply one conditional format to a raw A1 range.

        Registers get their conditional formats through ``grid`` via
        ``Col.cf``.  Pages that build their own grids - the booking
        calendar, mainly - need this instead.  It resolves the ``fmt``
        style name exactly as ``grid`` does, because passing a Format
        object under the key ``fmt`` is silently ignored by XlsxWriter
        and the colour just never appears.
        """
        options = dict(rule)
        fmt_key = options.pop("fmt", None)
        if fmt_key is not None:
            options["format"] = (self.f.cf(fmt_key)
                                 if isinstance(fmt_key, str)
                                 else fmt_key)
        if "criteria" in options and isinstance(options["criteria"], str):
            options["criteria"] = self.reg.render(
                options["criteria"]).strip()
        self.ws.conditional_format(cell_range, options)

    def formula(self, row: int, col: int, text: str, fmt=None):
        """Write a formula, resolving any ``[[Sheet.key]]`` tokens.

        The rendered text is stripped: Excel tolerates a stray space
        on the end of a formula but several calculation engines -
        including the one the recalculation check uses - refuse to
        parse it, and a space is the easiest thing in the world to
        leave behind when a formula is concatenated over ten lines of
        source.
        """
        self.ws.write_formula(row, col, self.reg.render(text).strip(), fmt)

    def merge(self, row: int, first_col: int, last_col: int, value: Any,
              fmt=None, row2: Optional[int] = None):
        row2 = row if row2 is None else row2
        if first_col == last_col and row == row2:
            self.write(row, first_col, value, fmt)
        else:
            text = "" if value is None else value
            if isinstance(text, (_dt.datetime, _dt.date, _dt.time)):
                self.ws.merge_range(row, first_col, row2, last_col, "", fmt)
                self.ws.write_datetime(row, first_col, text, fmt)
            else:
                self.ws.merge_range(row, first_col, row2, last_col, text, fmt)

    def set_col(self, first: int, last: int, width: float, fmt=None,
                hidden: bool = False):
        options = {"hidden": 1} if hidden else {}
        self.ws.set_column(first, last, width, fmt, options)

    def row_height(self, row: int, height: float):
        self.ws.set_row(row, height)

    # ----------------------------------------------------------- page chrome
    def banner(self, title: str, subtitle: str = "", last_col: int = 9,
               nav: bool = True, badge: str = "",
               tail_text: str = "") -> None:
        """Title row + strapline + navigation strip (Excel rows 1-3).

        `tail_text` is written in the empty space to the right of the
        navigation links - used for the register help line on sheets whose
        header row leaves no spare row for it.
        """
        r = TITLE_ROW - 1
        self.row_height(r, 34)
        split = max(last_col - 3, 1)
        self.merge(r, 0, split, title, self.f.chrome("title"))
        self.merge(r, split + 1, last_col,
                   badge or f"{self.cfg.author}  |  v{self.cfg.version}",
                   self.f.chrome("title_right"))

        r = SUBTITLE_ROW - 1
        self.row_height(r, 18)
        self.merge(r, 0, last_col, subtitle, self.f.chrome("subtitle"))

        if nav:
            self.nav_strip(NAV_ROW - 1, last_col, tail_text=tail_text)

    def nav_strip(self, row: int, last_col: int,
                  links: Optional[Sequence[Tuple[str, str]]] = None,
                  tail_text: str = "") -> int:
        """Row of internal links. Returns the first column left over."""
        links = list(links or NAV_LINKS)
        self.row_height(row, 16)
        col = 0
        fmt = self.f.chrome("nav")
        for label, sheet in links:
            if col + 1 > last_col:
                break
            self.ws.merge_range(row, col, row, min(col + 1, last_col), "", fmt)
            self.ws.write_url(row, col, f"internal:{quote_sheet(sheet)}!A1",
                              fmt, f"> {label}")
            col += 2
        if col <= last_col:
            room = last_col - col
            if tail_text and room >= 4:
                self.merge(row, col, last_col, tail_text,
                           self.f.chrome("note", bg_color=P.note_bg))
            else:
                self.merge(row, col, last_col, "",
                           self.f.chrome("nav_plain"))
        return col

    def section(self, row: int, text: str, last_col: int, first_col: int = 0):
        self.row_height(row, 20)
        self.merge(row, first_col, last_col, text, self.f.chrome("section"))
        return row + 1

    def subsection(self, row: int, text: str, last_col: int,
                   first_col: int = 0):
        self.row_height(row, 17)
        self.merge(row, first_col, last_col, text,
                   self.f.chrome("subsection"))
        return row + 1

    def note(self, row: int, text: str, last_col: int, first_col: int = 0,
             height: float = 28, boxed: bool = True):
        self.row_height(row, height)
        self.merge(row, first_col, last_col, text,
                   self.f.chrome("note_box" if boxed else "note"))
        return row + 1

    def bullets(self, row: int, lines: Sequence[str], last_col: int,
                first_col: int = 0, height: float = 15):
        for line in lines:
            self.row_height(row, height)
            self.merge(row, first_col, last_col, line, self.f.chrome("label"))
            row += 1
        return row

    # -------------------------------------------------------- settings rows
    def field(self, row: int, label: str, value: Any = None, *,
              label_col: int = 1, value_col: int = 3,
              value_end: Optional[int] = None, style: str = "text",
              mode: str = INPUT, name: Optional[str] = None,
              validate: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
              help_text: str = "", help_col: Optional[int] = None,
              formula: Optional[str] = None):
        """A `Label | value | help` settings row, optionally named."""
        self.merge(row, label_col, value_col - 1, label,
                   self.f.chrome("label_bold"))
        fmt = self.f.cell(style, mode)
        end = value_end if value_end is not None else value_col
        if formula is not None:
            rendered = self.reg.render(formula)
            if end > value_col:
                self.ws.merge_range(row, value_col, row, end, "", fmt)
            self.ws.write_formula(row, value_col, rendered, fmt)
        else:
            if end > value_col:
                self.merge(row, value_col, end, None, fmt)
                self.write(row, value_col, value, fmt)
            else:
                self.write(row, value_col, value, fmt)
        if validate:
            self.ws.data_validation(row, value_col, row, value_col, validate)
        if help_text:
            hc = help_col if help_col is not None else end + 1
            self.merge(row, hc, hc + 3, help_text, self.f.chrome("note"))
        if name:
            self.book.define_name(
                name, f"={quote_sheet(self.name)}!"
                      f"${col_letter(value_col)}${row + 1}")
        return row + 1

    # ------------------------------------------------------------ KPI tiles
    def kpi(self, row: int, col: int, label: str, formula: str,
            style: str = "int", span: int = 2, note: str = ""):
        """Three row KPI tile: caption, big number, small note."""
        self.merge(row, col, col + span - 1, label, self.f.chrome("kpi_label"))
        self.row_height(row + 1, 26)
        fmt = self.f.chrome("kpi_value",
                            num_format=self._num_format(style))
        if span > 1:
            self.ws.merge_range(row + 1, col, row + 1, col + span - 1,
                                "", fmt)
        self.ws.write_formula(row + 1, col, self.reg.render(formula), fmt)
        self.merge(row + 2, col, col + span - 1, note,
                   self.f.chrome("kpi_note"))
        return row + 3

    def num_format(self, style: str) -> str:
        """Number format string for a style key (public helper)."""
        return self._num_format(style)

    def _num_format(self, style: str) -> str:
        return {
            "money": self.cfg.money_format,
            "money0": self.cfg.money_format_0,
            "money4": self.cfg.money_format_4,
            "int": "#,##0",
            "number": "#,##0.00",
            "number1": "#,##0.0",
            "percent": "0.0%",
            "percent0": "0%",
            "date": self.cfg.date_format,
            "text": "General",
        }.get(style, "General")

    # ------------------------------------------------------- generic tables
    def table_head(self, row: int, col: int, headers: Sequence[str],
                   widths: Optional[Sequence[float]] = None,
                   align_left_first: bool = True):
        for i, head in enumerate(headers):
            fmt = self.f.chrome(
                "header_left" if (i == 0 and align_left_first) else "header")
            self.write(row, col + i, head, fmt)
            if widths:
                self.set_col(col + i, col + i, widths[i])
        self.row_height(row, 26)
        return row + 1

    def calc_row(self, row: int, col: int, values: Sequence[Any],
                 styles: Sequence[str], mode: str = CALC,
                 first_style: str = "text"):
        for i, value in enumerate(values):
            style = styles[i] if i < len(styles) else "text"
            fmt = self.f.cell(style, PLAIN if i == 0 and mode == PLAIN
                              else mode)
            if isinstance(value, str) and value.startswith("="):
                self.ws.write_formula(row, col + i, self.reg.render(value),
                                      fmt)
            else:
                self.write(row, col + i, value, fmt)
        return row + 1

    # ----------------------------------------------------------- the grid --
    def grid(self, spec: SheetSpec, extra_help: str = "") -> None:
        """Render a whole register sheet from its specification."""
        ws = self.ws
        last_col = spec.last_col_index
        header_row0 = spec.header_row - 1
        first = spec.first_data_row
        last = spec.last_data_row

        help_text = extra_help or spec.help_text
        spare_row = spec.header_row - 1 > NAV_ROW   # room above the headers?
        self.banner(spec.title, spec.subtitle, last_col,
                    tail_text="" if spare_row else help_text)

        if help_text and spare_row:
            self.note(header_row0 - 1, help_text, last_col, height=26)

        # Column widths, default formats (so blank cells keep the right lock
        # state) and the header row itself.
        for idx, col in enumerate(spec.columns):
            mode = CALC if col.is_formula else INPUT
            self.set_col(idx, idx, col.width, self.f.cell(col.style, mode),
                         hidden=col.hidden)
            self.write(header_row0, idx, col.header,
                       self.f.chrome("header_left" if idx <= 1 else "header"))
        self.row_height(header_row0, 30)

        # Data rows: formulas everywhere, sample values in the input columns.
        samples = spec.samples if self.cfg.include_sample_data else []
        for offset in range(spec.rows):
            excel_row = first + offset
            row0 = excel_row - 1
            sample = samples[offset] if offset < len(samples) else {}
            for idx, col in enumerate(spec.columns):
                if col.is_formula:
                    fmt = self.f.cell(col.style, CALC)
                    ws.write_formula(
                        row0, idx,
                        self.reg.render(col.formula, excel_row, spec), fmt)
                elif col.key in sample and sample[col.key] is not None:
                    self.write(row0, idx, sample[col.key],
                               self.f.cell(col.style, INPUT))

        # Drop downs, help bubbles and conditional formats.
        for idx, col in enumerate(spec.columns):
            if col.validate:
                options = dict(col.validate)
                if "source" in options and isinstance(options["source"], str):
                    options["source"] = self.reg.render(options["source"])
                if col.note:
                    options.setdefault("input_title", col.header[:32])
                    options.setdefault("input_message", col.note[:255])
                ws.data_validation(first - 1, idx, last - 1, idx, options)
            if col.note:
                # Header comment: works in every Excel version and survives
                # the trip through Google Sheets.
                ws.write_comment(header_row0, idx, col.note, {
                    "author": self.cfg.author,
                    "width": 220,
                    "height": 100,
                    "x_scale": 1.1,
                })
            for rule in col.cf:
                options = dict(rule)
                fmt_key = options.pop("fmt", None)
                if fmt_key:
                    options["format"] = self.f.cf(fmt_key)
                for field_name in ("criteria", "value", "minimum", "maximum"):
                    val = options.get(field_name)
                    if isinstance(val, str) and ("[[" in val or '{' in val):
                        options[field_name] = self.reg.render(
                            val, first, spec)
                ws.conditional_format(first - 1, idx, last - 1, idx, options)

        ws.autofilter(header_row0, 0, last - 1, last_col)
        freeze_row = (spec.freeze_at if spec.freeze_at is not None
                      else spec.header_row)
        ws.freeze_panes(freeze_row, spec.freeze_cols)
        ws.print_area(0, 0, last - 1, last_col)
        ws.repeat_rows(0, header_row0 if spec.header_row <= 6 else 2)
        ws.fit_to_pages(1, 0)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------- finishing
    def finish(self, freeze_row: Optional[int] = None,
               freeze_col: int = 0, print_area: Optional[str] = None,
               fit_width: bool = True, gridlines: bool = True):
        if freeze_row is not None:
            self.ws.freeze_panes(freeze_row, freeze_col)
        if print_area:
            self.ws.print_area(print_area)
        if fit_width:
            self.ws.fit_to_pages(1, 0)
        if not gridlines:
            self.ws.hide_gridlines(2)
        self.protect()

    def protect(self):
        if self.cfg.protect_sheets and not self._protected:
            self.ws.protect(self.cfg.password, dict(PROTECT_OPTIONS))
            self._protected = True


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Small shared helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def yes_no(validate_note: str = "") -> Dict[str, Any]:
    opts: Dict[str, Any] = {"validate": "list", "source": ["Yes", "No"]}
    if validate_note:
        opts["input_message"] = validate_note
    return opts


def list_from(name: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Drop down fed by a defined name (see lists.py)."""
    return {"validate": "list", "source": f"={name}"}


def date_check() -> Dict[str, Any]:
    return {
        "validate": "date",
        "criteria": "between",
        "minimum": _dt.date(2000, 1, 1),
        "maximum": _dt.date(2100, 12, 31),
        "error_title": "Check the date",
        "error_message": "Enter a real date between 2000 and 2100.",
    }


def time_check() -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Any time of day. Typing 9:00 AM or 14:30 both work."""
    return {
        "validate": "time",
        "criteria": "between",
        "minimum": _dt.time(0, 0),
        "maximum": _dt.time(23, 59),
        "error_title": "Check the time",
        "error_message": "Enter a time of day, for example 9:00 AM "
                         "or 14:30.",
    }


def number_check(minimum: float = 0, maximum: float = 1000000,
                 decimal: bool = True) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    return {
        "validate": "decimal" if decimal else "integer",
        "criteria": "between",
        "minimum": minimum,
        "maximum": maximum,
        "error_title": "Check the value",
        "error_message": f"Enter a number between {minimum} and {maximum}.",
    }


def cf_text(text: str, fmt: str, criteria: str = "containing") -> Dict[str, Any]:
    return {"type": "text", "criteria": criteria, "value": text, "fmt": fmt}


def cf_formula(formula: str, fmt: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    return {"type": "formula", "criteria": formula, "fmt": fmt}


def cf_bar(color: str = "#2E7D8F") -> Dict[str, Any]:
    return {"type": "data_bar", "bar_color": color}
````
